Wider Sports News.body:
Manchester United have agreed a training kit sponsorship deal with Betway, believed to be worth in excess of UK£20 million (US$27 million) a year. Betway become a ‘principal partner’ of the Premier League club as well as its exclusive global betting partner. The partnership covers both United’s men’s and women’s teams with Betway branding appearing at both Old Trafford and the Progress with Unity Stadium.

The partnership is understood to be the most valuable standalone training kit or sleeve partnership in world soccer. Several other European giants have comparable deals however these include other elements such as naming rights partnerships.

Wider Sports News.title: PFL’s merger with Jake Paul’s MVP is latest convergence of boxing and MMA but can it take on UFC?
Wider Sports News.summary: A new deal uniting Jake Paul’s MVP with MMA promoter Professional Fighters League reflects growing trends of scale and consolidation across once disparate combat sports disciplines. The post PFL’s merger with Jake Paul’s MVP is latest convergence of boxing and MMA but can it take on UFC? appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The Ultimate Fighting Championship’s (UFC) dominance of mixed martial arts (MMA) was once so great that it became synonymous with a sport that many believed could eventually rival boxing as the world’s most popular combat discipline.

But the advent of rival MMA promotions and a revival in prize fighting have done much to challenge these assumptions. Between shifting promotional alliances, rising regional powerbases, new media priorities and emerging sources of capital, change has become a constant in the combat sports business.

Wider Sports News.title: Beyond the Purse: Inside Golf Saudi’s US$15m strategy to reshape women’s golf
Wider Sports News.summary: As PIF London Championship nears, Golf Saudi's US$15m Global Series is redrawing the commercial blueprint for women's professional golf. The post Beyond the Purse: Inside Golf Saudi’s US$15m strategy to reshape women’s golf appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The global sports economy is changing, and women’s professional golf is leading the way. When the Ladies European Tour (LET) starts the PIF London Championship at Centurion Club in Hertfordshire from August 6 to 9, 2026, it will mark the sixth consecutive year of this event. This championship is more than just a top tournament; it represents a long-term strategy by Golf Saudi and the Public Investment Fund (PIF) aimed at transforming professional golf, creating inclusive communities, and making Saudi Arabia a centre for sports tourism.

For years, women’s professional sports faced challenges like limited funding, a lack of broadcast exposure, and fragmented sponsorship opportunities. Launched in 2021 as the Aramco Team Series, this initiative changed the situation by adding institutional support. Now part of the PIF Global Series, the LET’s financial foundation has been strengthened. For the 2026 season, the series will provide an unprecedented US$15 million in total prize money across five international events, giving an economic stability to the tour.

Wider Sports News.title: Beyond the purse: Inside Golf Saudi’s US$15m strategy to reshape women’s golf
Wider Sports News.summary: As PIF London Championship nears, Golf Saudi's US$15m Global Series is redrawing the commercial blueprint for women's professional golf. The post Beyond the purse: Inside Golf Saudi’s US$15m strategy to reshape women’s golf appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The global sports economy is changing, and women’s professional golf is leading the way. When the Ladies European Tour (LET) starts the PIF London Championship at Centurion Club in Hertfordshire from 6th to 9th August 6 2026, it will mark the sixth consecutive year of this event. This championship is more than just a top tournament; it represents a long-term strategy by Golf Saudi and the Public Investment Fund (PIF) aimed at transforming professional golf, creating inclusive communities, and making Saudi Arabia a centre for sports tourism.

For years, women’s professional sports faced challenges like limited funding, a lack of broadcast exposure, and fragmented sponsorship opportunities. Launched in 2021 as the Aramco Team Series, this initiative changed the situation by adding institutional support. Now part of the PIF Global Series, the LET’s financial foundation has been strengthened. For the 2026 season, the series will provide an unprecedented US$15 million in total prize money across five international events, providing the tour with economic stability.

Rugby.title: Why £1m-a-season deal will be hard for Pollock and Hearn to find
Rugby.summary: Salary cap regulations might not be high on everyone's holiday reading list, but Eddie Hearn might be interested if he's keen to get Henry Pollock's £1m pay-day.
Rugby.body:
Salary cap regulations might not be high on everyone's holiday reading list, but agent Eddie Hearn might be interested if he's keen to get Henry Pollock's £1m pay-day. The Prem salary cap is currently £6.4m per club. In basic terms, your whole squad's salaries have to add up to £6.4m or less.

There's an outside chance the Northampton back row could get a salary of £1m next season, if a club out there has that amount of space in the cap. The only team thought to be in this bracket, according to the last published salary cap report in 2024-25, would be Newcastle.

Rugby.body:
Former Ospreys lock Will Greatbanks has revealed that he is quitting rugby to pursue his dream job in yachting, with ambitions to become the captain of a multi-million-pound Superyacht.

Rugby.title: France international Thomas Ramos' shock transfer confirmed by Toulouse
Rugby.summary: France full-back Thomas Ramos has agreed to a shock move, swapping Toulouse for Racing 92 when his contract runs out at the end of the season.
Rugby.body:
France full-back Thomas Ramos has agreed to a shock move, swapping Toulouse for Racing 92 when his contract runs out at the end of the season, his current employers have confirmed.

The 52-cap international will move to the French capital after the World Cup in Australia next year, but remaisn committed to Les Rouges et Noir until then. “Thomas Ramos is one of the faces of Stade Toulousain. Beyond his immense talent, he is an exceptional competitor and a player whose high standards elevate the entire team,” said club president, Didier Lacroix.

Rugby.title: Babalwa Latsha talks Boks captaincy and the 'experience of a lifetime'
Rugby.summary: Babalwa Latsha knows the weight and magnitude of being a Springbok captain and she "excitedly" and "humbly" accepted the responsibility when Swys de Bruin named her as the team's new skipper in July.
Rugby.body:
Babalwa Latsha knows the weight and magnitude of being a Springbok captain and she “excitedly” and “humbly” accepted the responsibility when Swys de Bruin named her as the team’s new skipper in July.

Latsha takes over from her close friend Nolusindiso Booi, who she says has helped shape her as a leader. The 32-year-old’s first games in charge as official captain was South Africa’s tied two-Test series against the USA Women’s Eagles.

Rugby.title: Newcastle sign Fiji hooker Togiatama
Rugby.summary: Newcastle Red Bulls sign Fiji hooker Zuriel Togiatama on a one-year deal.
Rugby.body:
Newcastle Red Bulls have signed Fiji hooker Zuriel Togiatama on a one-year deal. The 27-year-old joins the Prem side from Super Rugby outfit Fijian Drua. "He has proven himself at both Super Rugby and international level, is strong in the set-piece, carries the ball with real intent and has the work rate and physicality that are so important for a hooker," head coach Dan McFarland told the club website., external

Rugby.title: McMillan retires from international rugby five months after Scotland recall
Rugby.summary: Louise McMillan has announced her retirement from international rugby five months after her return to the Scotland set-up.
Rugby.body:
Louise McMillan has announced her retirement from international rugby five months after her return to the Scotland set-up. Across a decade long Test career McMillan earned 61 caps, but missed out on a year of international rugby after she was dropped from the Scotland squad ahead of Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 by then-head coach Bryan Easson.

Performances for JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby club Saracens, with whom she will continue playing domestic rugby for, earned McMillan a recall and three final caps for her country at this year’s Guinness Women’s Six Nations. Her final cap came in Scotland’s 54-5 loss to Ireland at Dublin’s Aviva Stadium.

Rugby.title: The teenage Cardiff hooker ignoring Wales hype
Rugby.summary: Hooker Tom Howe stays grounded after being tipped as one to watch for Wales before his debut for Cardiff.
Rugby.body:
Others might believe it is a matter of time before he wins his first Wales cap, but hooker Tom Howe is more concerned with trying to make his Cardiff debut. The 18-year-old is enjoying a well-earned rest after his exploits with Wales Under-20s at the Junior World Championship.

The 6ft 3in front-row forward made four starts when helping Richard Whiffen's side finish sixth, featuring prominently with 28 carries and 54 tackles alongside solid set-piece work.

Rugby.title: Two Englishmen on referee panel for Greatest Rivalry Series
Rugby.summary: A four-strong referee panel has been named for the Gretest Rivalry Series, including the four provincial tour matches.
Rugby.body:
The four referees for the Greatest Rivalry Series between South Africa and New Zealand have been announced by World Rugby, with Matt Carley taking charge of the first Test at Ellis Park in Johannesburg on 22 August.

Groundbreaking Georgian official Nika Amashukeli has been handed the second Test at the DHL Stadium Cape Town a week later, while Australian official Angus Gardner will run the rule over the third Test, which takes place at the FNB Stadium in Johannesburg on 5 September.

Rugby.title: South African rugby 'family secret' adds extra spice to Boks vs All Blacks series
Rugby.summary: Great rivalries need more than close matches. They need inherited grievance, disputed memories and old wounds that can be pressed for fun. They need a little bad blood.
Rugby.body:
Does your family have a secret? A rumour that, if it were true, would shatter relationships? Perhaps an extra-marital affair or a link to organised crime. Maybe your uncle really is a gambling addict. What if your gran really did embezzle from that nursing home?

Best not to think about it. No need to air the dirty laundry. Pour yourself another drink and make small talk with your cousins. Why let the truth get in the way of a good time?

Rugby.summary: Scotland have been able to recall a number of senior forwards upon the announcement of their WXV Global Series squad.
Rugby.body:
Scotland have been able to recall a number of senior forwards upon the announcement of their WXV Global Series squad. Rachel Malcolm, who missed three matches at the 2026 Guinness Women’s Six Nations, returns to the squad as captain. As does Evie Gallagher, Sarah Bonar and Anne Young, who each missed the entire Championship with injury.

This squad has been named just 24 hours after the bombshell confirmation that Sione Fukofuka has left his post as head coach just shy of eight months in the role. Dave Butcher will lead Scotland as interim head coach.

Rugby.title: Three-time Super Rugby winning head coach will lead Fiji into new era
Rugby.summary: Three-time Super Rugby Aupiki winning head coach Willie Walker has signed on to be head coach of Fiji Women.
Rugby.body:
Three-time Super Rugby Aupiki winning head coach Willie Walker has signed on to be head coach of Fiji Women. Walker has enjoyed established success with the Blues Women in New Zealand since Super Rugby Aupiki’s establishment in 2021, and led them to consecutive titles in 2024, 2025 and 2026.

The 48-year-old concluded his time at the Blues with a win over the NSW Waratahs in a close-fought Super Rugby Champions final in Sydney. Walker said: “It is a privilege to be entrusted with leading the Vodafone Fijiana XV. Fiji has an incredible rugby culture and a talented group of athletes with enormous potential.

Rugby.summary: Brooke played for the All Blacks between 1987 and 1997, appearing in 58 Tests and scoring 195 points, made up of 42 tries and three drop goals.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks legend Zinzan Brooke knows what it takes to win a Test series in South Africa with his dramatic second Test drop goal in 1996 ensuring victory over the Springboks and providing the backdrop for the impending four-Test series between the world’s top two teams that is set to captivate the sport.

The All Blacks start their first tour of South Africa for 30 years against the Stormers on Friday with the double World Cup-while the Springboks completed their warm-up for the Test series by taking on Argentina in Buenos Aires on Saturday.

Rugby.title: All Blacks-Springboks series a battle of slow versus fast
Rugby.summary: Although they have fast athletes out wide, South Africa are playing a slow game with the ball, and you can assume they want it officiated that way. The All Blacks, on the other hand, want the opposite.
Rugby.body:
Do the Springboks really want to play a fast game? The answer to that question still has not been provided to us despite evolving their game significantly since 2023. South Africa have aligned themselves with the northern hemisphere club game, but they like to ‘feel’ like they belong in the southern hemisphere. At some point, the integration with Europe becomes ingrained.

The game speed in the northern hemisphere is slower, despite ball-in-play time being comparable across the leagues. High ball-in-play time doesn’t automatically equal fast. Down in the south, Super Rugby Pacific has pushed forward with stripping out dead time in a fixture, stricter time limits on scrum setting, and more freedom on quick tap plays, while the officiating style differs drastically to continue the flow of a game.

Rugby.title: ‘Instinctive, confident, accurate’: The Cam Roigard mindset
Rugby.summary: Cam Roigard had just 40 minutes of experience in the Test arena when he was named in the All Blacks’ 2023 Rugby World Cup squad, but there would be no accusations of a fish out of water among New Zealand’s No.9 stocks.
Rugby.body:
Cam Roigard had just 40 minutes of experience in the Test arena when he was named in the All Blacks’ 2023 Rugby World Cup squad, but there would be no accusations of a fish out of water among New Zealand’s No.9 stocks.

Instead, Roigard’s performances at the tournament would verify the then-22-year-old’s immense potential and challenge Finlay Christie’s role as the Robin to Aaron Smith’s Batman. Sure enough, the following Test season saw the beginning of a new era in the black No.9 jersey; Roigard left France having proven himself Smith’s successor, bringing a new X-factor to a jersey Smith had made his own over 12 seasons and 125 Tests.

Rugby.title: Why Wallabies star considers McReight one of world’s best openside flankers
Rugby.summary: Wallabies backrower Rob Valetini believes teammate Fraser McReight is one of the world’s best openside flankers.
Rugby.body:
Wallabies backrower Rob Valetini believes teammate Fraser McReight is one of the world’s best openside flankers, outlining the Queensland skipper’s relentless work rate and influence behind the scenes with the national team.

Rugby World Cup winner Jeremy Paul said on The Good, The Bad & The Rugby in October 2024 that McReight was “the best seven in the world currently.” The Wallaby is now 42 Tests into his international career and continues to tun heads in a world-renowned loose forwards trio.

Rugby.title: There will be no All Blacks XV tour in 2026
Rugby.summary: New Zealand Rugby has confirmed its national development team, the All Blacks XV, will not tour this year.
Rugby.body:
New Zealand Rugby (NZR) has confirmed its national development team, the All Blacks XV, will not tour this year. The decision was made after considering the development opportunities of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Tour, which has taken an expanded squad of 44 players to South Africa and the USA.

In a statement to RugbyPass, the governing body also noted the value of players competing in the NPC, which is often stripped of its top talent just before the playoffs, when the All Blacks and All Blacks XV squads depart for the usual November fixtures.

Rugby.title: North Queensland Schoolgirls Rugby Sevens Signs Off in Style — A Season to Remember
Rugby.summary: North Queensland Schoolgirls Rugby Sevens Signs Off in Style — A Season to Remember Queensland Rugby Union
Rugby.body:
The curtain has come down on the inaugural NQ Schoolgirls Super 7s Series, and what a season it has been. Round 4 — held in Bowen on Wednesday — brought a fitting and spectacular conclusion to a competition that has exceeded every expectation, grown with every round, and firmly established itself as one of the most exciting developments in North Queensland rugby.

From Townsville to Bowen and everywhere in between, schoolgirls rugby sevens in the north is alive, thriving, and heading somewhere very special. The Under 14s competition was fiercely contested across all four rounds, with four schools giving absolutely everything on the park. When the overall points tally was finalised, it was St Margaret Mary's College who took home the series honours — a well-deserved reward for a team that delivered consistently and brilliantly across the competition.

Rugby.title: Waratahs sign reigning Super Rugby AUS Player of the Tournament
Rugby.summary: Versatile playmaker Max Burey has sealed a move from the Western Force to the NSW Waratahs, signing a two-year deal.
Rugby.body:
Versatile playmaker Max Burey has sealed a move from the Western Force to the NSW Waratahs, with the reigning Super Rugby AUS Player of the Tournament making the move east on a two-year deal until the end of 2028.

Wagga Wagga-born Burey returns home to New South Wales after making 37 Super Rugby Pacific appearances for the Force, and starring during the team’s run to the maiden Super Rugby AUS Grand Final last October.

Rugby.summary: Former Wallabies squad member Trevor Hosea is returning home to Australia on a two-year deal with the Western Force.
Rugby.body:
Former Wallabies squad member Trevor Hosea is returning home to Australia on a two-year deal with the Western Force, bolstering the squad’s depth in the second row after the departures of Darcy Swain and Franco Molina.

Hosea became a mainstay of the Melbourne Rebels starting side from 2018 to 2023, which led to higher honours in the Wallabies squad. Dave Rennie included Hosea in a squad for a Gold Coast camp in 2021, but the 204-centimetre lock remains an uncapped prospect.

Rugby.summary: While there is plenty of competition across the team, a highly talented loose forward unit is perhaps the most likely to give selectors headaches.
Rugby.body:
Forty-four of New Zealand’s finest are in Cape Town ahead of the opening match of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Tour, with four warm-up fixtures against URC outfits offering players the opportunity to stake their claim on a place in the matchday 23 for the historic four-Test series.

While there is plenty of competition across the team, a highly talented loose forward unit is perhaps the most likely to give selectors headaches, featuring eight players competing for just three starting positions and one, or potentially two, bench roles.

Rugby.body:

The Highlanders and Jamie Joseph have added two internationals to their 2027 Super Rugby Pacific squad, with Samoan outside back Tuna Tuitama and Fijian lock Joseva Tamani joining the Dunedin-based franchise.

Tuitama moves south from Moana Pasifika, where he made nine appearances for the Super Rugby franchise, and thirteen for Samoa since making his debut in 2024. The outside back previously starred for the Fijian HSBC SVNS Series team, scoring 30 tries in 56 appearances.

Rugby.summary: “My time at the Blues has been an amazing adventure and I know that I will always be a part of this club in some capacity,” the departing head coach said.
Rugby.body:
Three-time Super Rugby Aupiki championship-winning head coach Willie Walker has announced his departure from the Blues, after six seasons at the helm. The Blues head coach will leave the franchise after three straight Super Rugby Aupiki titles and back-to-back Women’s Super Rugby Champions Finals triumphs.

Walker’s announcement comes only a couple of days after their latest title, overcoming a tough NSW Waratahs side at Leichardt Oval to become 2026 Women’s Super Rugby Champions yet again, a week after their Aupiki championship.

Rugby.title: Former England prop and Exeter coach Robin Cowling dies, aged 82
Rugby.summary: Capped eight times by England in the 1970s, Cowling won four National Cups, one with Gloucester and three with Leicester.
Rugby.body:
Former England prop Robin Cowling has died aged 82 after a lifetime devoted to rugby. Capped eight times by England in the 1970s, Cowling won four National Cups, one with Gloucester and three with Leicester, as well as playing in four County Championship finals for Gloucestershire.

Cowling made his international debut in a 26-6 win over Scotland in 1977, in a front row containing Peter Wheeler and Fran Cotton. He credited the move to Leicester in 1974 for the improvements that led to Test recognition.

Rugby.title: Exeter stalwart Cowling dies aged 82
Rugby.summary: Former Exeter Chiefs coach and Leicester Tigers and Gloucester player Robin Cowling dies aged 82.
Rugby.body:
Former Exeter Chiefs coach Robin Cowling has died aged 82. The England international prop joined Exeter in 1998 as a coach and had a spell as interim team manager in 2009 following the sacking of director of rugby Pete Drewett, before current team boss Rob Baxter took over later that year.

Cowling worked with Exeter's academy and was instrumental in helping bring through a generation of talented young players including Jack Nowell, Luke Cowan-Dickie, Neil Clarke, Jason Hobson, Ben Moon and Jack Yeandle.

Rugby.title: Cilliers headlines 30-player South Africa 'A' squad that will travel to Brazil
Rugby.summary: A total of nine capped Springbok Women have been included in a SA Women's 'A' squad that will travel to Brazil at the end of August.
Rugby.body:
A total of nine capped Springbok Women have been included in a SA Women’s ‘A’ squad that will travel to Brazil at the end of August. The 30-player Springbok Women Academy will gather for two camps in Somerset West before 26 players travel to South America to take on Brazil’s senior side on Monday 24 and Saturday 29 August in Brasilia and Sao Paulo.

Rugby Club Toulon Provence Méditerranée-bound back Jakkie Cilliers has been named in the squad as have fellow senior internationals Anusckha Ekron, Luchell Hanekom, Abigail Smit, Sino Bhengu, Zethu Gcaza, Insaaf Levy, Mary Zulu and Shaunique Alexander.

Rugby.title: Pollock to demand £1m a year at Northampton
Rugby.summary: Henry Pollock is set to demand a substantial increase on his current Northampton contract to stay at Franklin's Gardens, with agent Eddie Hearn suggesting annual earnings of £1m are his going rate.
Rugby.body:
Henry Pollock is set to demand a substantial increase on his current Northampton contract to stay at Franklin's Gardens, with agent Eddie Hearn suggesting annual earnings of £1m are the going rate for the 21-year-old star.

"He's certainly a seven-figure player," said Hearn, who met with Pollock on his yacht off Monaco last month, to the Daily Telegraph., external "The way rugby's going and what Pollock is doing, his value over the next couple of years will skyrocket, and I think the value of rugby will."

Rugby.title: Ex-Wallaroos captain Hamilton signs on with Élite 1's Toulon
Rugby.summary: Former Wallaroos skipper Grace Hamilton has signed for AXA Élite 1 club Rugby Club Toulon Provence Méditerranée ahead of the 2026/27 season.
Rugby.body:
Former Wallaroos skipper Grace Hamilton has signed for AXA Élite 1 club Rugby Club Toulon Provence Méditerranée ahead of the 2026/27 season. The 34-year-old back-row forward, who represented Australia at Women’s Rugby World Cup 2017 and 2021, joins the French club after a year with SG Valley RFC in Hong Kong China.

Hamilton has also represented the ACT Brumbies, NSW Waratahs and Melbourne Rebels in Super Rugby Women’s, as well as the Sydney Roosters and St George Illawarra Dragons in NRLW. She also enjoyed a previous spell in Élite 1 with Montpellier in 2023/24.

Rugby.title: Make in-demand Henry Pollock a millionaire, urges Eddie Hearn
Rugby.summary: Pollock is in the last year of his contract at Northampton Saints.
Rugby.body:
Eddie Hearn has urged Northampton Saints to offer England star Henry Pollock a new seven-figure deal to keep him at Franklin’s Gardens beyond the end of the season. Pollock, who opened talks with Saints about a new deal at the end of the last campaign as his current contract only has a year left to run, joined boxing promotor Hearn’s Matchroom Talent Agency in March and has seen his commercial value rocket over the last few months.

But because nothing was agreed by June 30th, it’s enabled rival clubs from the Gallagher PREM and Top 14 to come in and try to entice one of the games brightest talents away from the reigning PREM champions.

Rugby.summary: Glasgow have announced a 20-strong senior academy intake for the 2026/27 season, which includes the Mackenzie brothers.
Rugby.body:
Glasgow Warriors’ 20-strong senior academy intake for the 2026/27 season includes highly-rated South African-born, Scottish-qualified twins, James and Josh Mckenzie. James is a utility back, while Josh, who has played for the SA Schools U18s side, is a versatile forward who can play across the back five of the scrum.

Eligible for Scotland through their paternal grandparents, the brothers caught the eye during the Warriors’ United Rugby Championship tour of South Africa in April, training with the squad while in Johannesburg.

Rugby.title: Northampton sign Italian international Neculai
Rugby.summary: Northampton Saints sign Italian International tighthead prop Ion Neculai from Zebre.
Rugby.body:
Northampton Saints have signed Italian international tight-head prop Ion Neculai from Italian club Zebre Parma. The 25‑year‑old joins the Prem champions after five seasons with Zebre, where he made 51 appearances.

Neculai joins former Zebre team‑mate Malik Faissal in moving to Franklin's Gardens this summer, while Danilo Fischetti transferred in 2025. Neculai has four senior Italy caps, earning his latest last month in Perth when he came off the bench during his side's 57-10 defeat against Australia in the Nations Championship.

Rugby.summary: Emirates match officials have been announced for the six women's internationals taking place between August and October.
Rugby.body:
Emirates match officials have been announced for the six women’s internationals taking place between August and October. Across the next fortnight Australian pair Jess Ling and Amber McLachlan will officiate the two-Test series between the Fijiana XV and South Africa in Suva and Lautoka. Fixtures take place on Saturday 8 August and Saturday 15 August between the two nations.

New Zealand’s Maggie Cogger-Orr will officiate the second O’Reilly Cup clash of 2026 when the Black Ferns take on the Wallaroos on Saturday 22 August. Zoe Naude [South Africa] will referee the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry encounter between the Springbok Women and Black Ferns at Johannesburg’s FNB Stadium. The fixture forms part of a doubleheader.

Rugby.title: Red Roses make 'lethal exciting rugby' promise as WXV Global Series training squad announced
Rugby.summary: England's Red Roses have announced a 40-player training squad that will begin preparations for the WXV Global Series this week.
Rugby.body:
England’s Red Roses have announced a 40-player training squad that will begin preparations for the WXV Global Series this week. John Mitchell’s squad is comprised of 22 forwards and 18 backs, and will gather at the University of Nottingham on Monday 3 August to begin a three week preseason training stint.

There are six uncapped players in the squad; Bryony Field, Keevy Fitzpatrick, Hayley Jones, Annabel Meta, Amelia MacDougall and Carmela Morrall. Field took part in each of Saracens’ league fixtures last season as the club claimed the English league title.

Rugby.body:
Northampton’s Italian connection has been strengthened further with the signature of Azzurri international Ion Neculai. Neculai is the second Italian international to sign for the Saints this summer, following wing Malik Faissal, who made his Test debut against Japan in the Nations Championship and won his second cap against New Zealand a week later.

With Danilo Fischetti and Edoardo Todaro already in the squad, it makes for a four-strong Italian contingent at Franklin’s Gardens. Neculai, a Moldovan-born tight-head, joins Saints from Zebre Parma, where he made 51 appearances across five seasons.

Rugby.title: 'Family stress' forces Scotland boss Fukofuka to step down
Rugby.summary: Sione Fukofuka steps down from his role as Scotland Women head coach because of "the stress and the strain" of being apart from his family in Australia.
Rugby.body:
Sione Fukofuka has stepped down from his role as Scotland Women head coach because of "the stress and the strain" of being apart from his family in Australia. Forwards coach Dave Butcher will take over in interim charge as the side prepare for the start of the WXV Global Series.

Fukofuka, who was United States head coach between 2023 and 2025, was appointed late last year and led Scotland during the Women's Six Nations. "I've had to make probably the hardest professional decision of my life to step away from the role," he told the Scottish Rugby website., external

Rugby.body:
Sione Fukofuka has left his role as Scotland Women head coach eights months after his appointment by Scottish Rugby. The former prop has returned to Australia, citing family and personal reasons for his departure. At Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025, Fukofuka led a star-studded USA Women’s Eagles side to a group stage finish and previously coached Australia’s Wallaroos.

Fukofuka coached Scotland to a fifth-place finish at the 2026 Guinness Women’s Six Nations and one win, which came against Wales in Round 1. Fukofuka said: “I’ve had to make probably the hardest professional decision of my life to step away from the role as head coach.

Rugby.summary: Ex-All Black winger Jeff Wilson believes that Richie Mo'unga has settled as an insurance option for the All Blacks during the South African tour.
Rugby.body:
Ex-All Black winger Jeff Wilson believes that Richie Mo’unga has settled as an insurance option for the All Blacks during the South African tour, with the returning No.10 currently surplus to requirements.

Mo’unga played his first game back in New Zealand for Canterbury against Auckland in the Hilux NPC on Friday night, coming off the bench for a game-winning cameo. After entering the field the 32-year-old is now eligible for the All Blacks but with the squad already in South Africa preparing to play the Stormers in Cape Town, it is looking unlikely Mo’unga will be called upon.

Rugby.summary: "It'll bring the best out of Codie and he'll rise to that. But I actually really like the role of what what I saw from Asafo Aumua off the bench."
Rugby.body:
Three former All Blacks have discussed whether stand-in captain Codie Taylor deserves a starting spot in the first Test of the Greatest Rivalry Tour against South Africa. Taylor, an All Black centurion, has been given the role of “tour captain” and will lead Dave Rennie’s side in all of the off-field roles until Ardie Savea returns to the frame ahead of the first Test.

But there are still question marks from some whether, on form, Taylor deserves a starting spot over the likes of Hurricanes hooker Asafo Aumua and Chiefs enforcer Samisoni Taukei’aho.

Rugby.summary: Former All Black captain Kieran Read has identified a tactical weakness in the forward pack that he believes will be exploited by South Africa if they don't address it.
Rugby.body:
Former All Black captain Kieran Read has identified a tactical weakness in the forward pack that he believes will be exploited by South Africa if they don’t address it. The No.8 believes the balance is out of kilter in the carry game leading to an over-reliance on tight five forwards instead of the back five.

He identified lock Sam Darry as one of the All Blacks busiest forwards over the three games in July, but warned against having the young lock take the same work load against the Springboks.

Rugby.summary: “So his job is to go away, keep working hard, be ready if an opportunity arises. I’d be surprised that we don’t call someone out at some stage.”
Rugby.body:
Hurricanes co-captain Du’Plessis Kirifi has bounced back after a tough seven days, starring for Wellington in their 52-33 loss against Hawke’s Bay on Sunday afternoon at Hnry Stadium in Wellington.

The openside flanker will feel hard done by after missing out on the All Blacks squad for the Greatest Rivalry Tour, which included 44 players. But the Super Rugby Pacific 2026 winning co-captain didn’t let that get in the way of his first performance in the Hilux NPC competition, claiming three turnovers and a try in Wellington’s 19-point loss.

Rugby.summary: Northland are second after pulling clear of Manawatu 40-14. All Blacks Sevens winger Brady Rush touched down twice.
Rugby.body:
The 50th NPC began as it did in 1976, with Bay of Plenty beaten. Can the Steamers recover to take the title as they did in that inaugural season? Despite a noteworthy display from No.8 Nikora Broughton, who topped the meters carried count, scored a try, and added 23 tackles, it wasn’t enough to overhaul a hot Waikato start, 38-26. Opposing No.8 Malachi Wrampling-Alec and the electric Ollie Mathis were just as compelling.

Canterbury and Auckland christened Te Kaka/One New Zealand Stadium by producing a classic in Christchurch’s new rugby cathedral. Defending champions Canterbury narrowly prevailed 38-31 with Super Rugby Pacific winners Jamie Hannah, Dominic Gardiner, Corey Kellow and Jone Rova scoring tries and delivering the goods.

Rugby.title: Italy 7s international Ratko Jelic makes SuperLiga Kaufland switch
Rugby.summary: Italian 7s international Ratko Jelic has agreed to join SuperLiga Kaufland side Dinamo Bucharest, with the scrum-half expected to make his debut in the following weeks.
Rugby.body:
Italian 7s international Ratko Jelic has agreed to join SuperLiga Kaufland side Dinamo Bucharest, with the scrum-half expected to make his debut in the following weeks. Born in Belgrade, Jelic left Serbia at a young age and took his first steps in rugby at Rugby Jesi 1970, the same club his father played for in the 2000s.

He would eventually be enlisted in the Italian union academy system, but due to the COVID pandemic, Jelic missed the chance to represent the Azzurri U20s. Despite that setback, the scrum-half secured his first senior contract with Rugby Viadana, remaining with the Serie A Elite side until 2022, when he earned a move to Zebre.

Rugby.summary: Dutch side RC The Dukes has clinched Niall Saunders' services, with the former U20 Irish international joining the side for the upcoming Ereklasse season.
Rugby.body:
Dutch side RC The Dukes has clinched Niall Saunders’ services, with the former U20 Irish international joining the side for the upcoming Ereklasse season. The 28-year-old had been without a club for the past 20 months after his contract with RFC Los Angeles was terminated ahead of the 2025 season.

Saunders’ life in the pro leagues started in 2016, when Harlequins recruited the young scrum-half. In the same year, he won his first Ireland caps, representing the U20 side at the World Rugby Under-20 Championship, where Ireland reached the final but were defeated 45-21 by England.

Rugby.title: 'This isn't a walkover': Renewed hope for rivalry with Black Ferns following Trans-Tasman clash
Rugby.summary: But a gripping clash between the most dominant rugby franchises on both sides of the Tasman has spawned hope new talent can invigorate the rivalry.
Rugby.body:
In 29 games of women’s international rugby, Australia has never beaten New Zealand. But a gripping clash between the most dominant rugby franchises on both sides of the Tasman has spawned hope new talent can invigorate the rivalry.

The NSW Waratahs thoroughly spooked the Auckland Blues in the showdown of Super Rugby champions at Sydney’s Leichhardt Oval on Saturday. The firm underdogs, and having been thumped 36-5 in their last meeting, the Waratahs dominated lengthy passages of play and walked off the field only seven points in arrears (24-17) to hand the Blues their second straight title.

Rugby.title: Leicester back row Ilione out until 2027
Rugby.summary: Leicester Tigers back row Emeka Ilione is ruled out with a shoulder problem until "at least" the end of 2026.
Rugby.body:
Leicester Tigers back row Emeka Ilione has been ruled out until "at least" the end of 2026. The 24-year-old has not played since January because of a shoulder injury. Meanwhile, lock Harry Palmer, 20, will not feature until November after undergoing a knee operation.

"Unfortunately, Emeka's shoulder injury is complex and hasn't recovered as we hoped," head coach Geoff Parling told the club website., external "He will see the specialist again in November, but for now we know that he will be out until at least the New Year."

Rugby.title: Blues hold nerve as Tahs fall achingly short of trans-Tasman glory
Rugby.summary: The NSW Waratahs have fallen agonisingly short of pulling off a stunning upset, with the Auckland Blues prevailing in the clash of the Super Rugby Champions.
Rugby.body:
The NSW Waratahs have fallen agonisingly short of pulling off a stunning upset, with the Auckland Blues prevailing in the clash of the Super Rugby Champions. The Waratahs lost their bid for trans-Tasman glory in a thrilling contest with the Blues at Leichhardt Oval on Saturday, which was finally settled 24-17 in a match where momentum swung wildly from start to finish.

Despite impressive performances against the Western Force (33-22) and the Fijian Drua (34-17) to clinch a three-peat and their seventh Super Rugby Women’s title, the Waratahs had entered the contest with the New Zealand champions the clear underdogs.

Rugby.title: Richie Mo'unga completes dream Canterbury homecoming with game-winner
Rugby.summary: It was a tight 80 minutes, but turned into a dream homecoming for the 56-Test All Black when he darted over for a game-winning try in the 77th minute.
Rugby.body:
One New Zealand Stadium hosted its first NPC game as the centrepiece of the 2026 opening round, with traditional rivals Auckland and Canterbury squaring off under the roof. The match was most notable for the long-awaited return of Richie Mo’unga, who suited up for his first minutes of NPC since 2020 and officially regained his All Blacks eligibility with his first steps onto the pitch in the 51st minute.

It was a tight 80 minutes, but turned into a dream homecoming for the 56-Test All Black when he darted over for a game-winning try in the 77th minute. A Kurtis MacDonald break saw the big Canterbury winger burst through a tackle before getting dragged down, with a complementary incision by Chay Fihaki furthering momentum before Tahlor Cahill was given the ball unmarked on the right edge.

Rugby.title: Stand-in All Blacks captain Codie Taylor on Ardie Savea: 'He deserves a break'
Rugby.summary: Codie Taylor says Ardie Savea's belated arrival in South Africa for the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry Tour is a deserved rest for the All Blacks captain.
Rugby.body:
Codie Taylor says Ardie Savea’s belated arrival in South Africa for the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Tour is a deserved rest for the All Blacks captain. Standing in for Savea for the opening matches of the tour while the 2023 World Rugby Player of the Year enjoys some more downtime with family in New Zealand, Taylor and his troops were welcomed in Cape Town to begin their historic tour on Friday.

There will be eight games over seven weeks, including two midweek games and a series finale in the USA. Taylor will take charge of the opening three fixtures, against the Stormers, Sharks and Bulls, before Savea rejoins the squad ahead of the opening Test against the Springboks in Johannesburg.

Rugby.title: Addressing the 'obvious place to start' in Les Kiss' Wallabies evolution
Rugby.summary: It was clear from day one that defence was to change under new Wallabies head coach Les Kiss, and he has immediately demanded a new mindset for his defensive game plan.
Rugby.body:
It was clear from day one that defence was to change under new Wallabies head coach Les Kiss, and he has immediately demanded a new mindset for his defensive game plan. “One thing is for certain, that we want to make sure that we make it a weapon for us, so we can attack with it,” said Kiss after revealing his first-ever Wallabies squad at Allianz Stadium in Sydney.

“We are gonna take small steps; we don’t want to go in and change everything, or make massive change, we want to make sure we make the right steps.” While nothing has actually been said about how the Wallabies will defend, you should take Kiss’s words here to mean one thing: physicality.

Rugby.title: 'There will always be a place for the short, stocky, grubby, hard-nosed seven'
Rugby.summary: Lucas Rumball has played 66 Tests for Canada, including the 2019 Rugby World Cup, where he faced the All Blacks and eventual champions South Africa.
Rugby.body:
Lucas Rumball has played 66 Tests for Canada, including the 2019 Rugby World Cup, where he faced the All Blacks and eventual champions South Africa. The openside flanker has captained his country multiple times and is well positioned to comment on the zeitgeist of contemporary flanker play, which seems to prefer tall and versatile backrowers over the classic shorter scavenging seven. Are international prospects over for players like Du’Plessis Kirifi?

“The game is always shifting. Right now there are many high ball contests and a greater emphasis on offence where taller, faster athletes are preferred,” Rumball told RugbyPass.

Rugby.body:
Scarlets say they intend to remain "at the heart of west Wales" after being plunged into in a battle for survival with Ospreys by Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) plans. Welsh rugby's governing body has given the timeframe for their plans to cut its four professional teams to three by 2028, and confirmed on Wednesday that Cardiff and Dragons will be given licences.

That leaves Llanelli-based Scarlets and Swansea-based Ospreys fighting to be the side in the west, unless there is to be a merger. "It is our mission, as it has always been, to be at the forefront of a strong, meaningful and sustainable future for rugby in west Wales. Our focus remains unchanged and unhindered," said Scarlets in a message to supporters.

Several senior players, including Cheslin Kolbe, Damian Willemse, Jesse Kriel and Ruan Nortje, will remain in South Africa and reassemble in Johannesburg on Sunday ahead of preparations for the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Tour against New Zealand.

Rugby.title: Simon Middleton column: How the Red Roses created abundant player depth
Rugby.summary: How do the other nations catch England? Or can the other nations catch England?
Rugby.body:
How do the other nations catch England? Or can the other nations catch England? And if they can’t, or can’t even close the gap significantly, then what of the game as a competitive spectacle? Those are the questions currently being asked in women’s international rugby.

Whilst it may not be possible to answer those questions conclusively, I think it’s fair to say that unless the current crop of international teams can find a way to start producing more quality players and more quickly than they currently are, then the answer will be, no.

Rugby.title: Rugby v cricket
Rugby.summary: England and Saracens' Jamie George on why he and Somerset's Lewis Gregory are playing a charity cricket match to raise money for motor neurone disease charities.
Rugby.body:
Rugby might be England and Saracens hooker Jamie George's first love but cricket is still a regular part of his sporting life and career. It's why he and his club team-mates did not need much persuading to sign up for a rugby versus cricket T20 match against some of the County Championship's top professionals in August, to raise money for the Motor Neurone Disease Association.

"We [Saracens] do play [cricket] - our warm-up [for] every rugby session - summer, winter, snowing, rain - is one hand, one bounce," George told BBC Radio Somerset. "The boys love it because they're mad-keen cricket fans."

Rugby.title: England prospect Nathan Jibulu signs new long-term deal
Rugby.summary: England A hooker Nathan Jibulu has signed a contract extension with Sale Sharks that will see him remain with the club until at least 2030.
Rugby.body:
England A hooker Nathan Jibulu has signed a contract extension with Sale Sharks that will see him remain with the club until at least 2030. The London-born front-rower played 23 games for Sharks in his first season at the club after joining from Harlequins ahead of the 2025/26 season, and would have played more had he not been hit with a six-game ban for biting in a match against his former club.

The 23-year-old had one year remaining on his first Sharks contract but was more than happy to commit to a longer-term deal. “I’ve loved my first year at Sale. The boys are so together on and off the pitch. We all see each other away from Carrington and that’s been brilliant,” said Jibulu.

Rugby.summary: Club historian Neil Williams has dipped into his treasure trove of stats and uncovered another gem.
Rugby.body:
From the very first, Wallace Jarman in 1900, 288 different players have gained a full international cap whilst playing for Bristol. This includes six who were retrospectively awarded a cap earlier this year, including club legend Nigel Pomphrey.

George Kloska became the most recent addition to the list when he made his England debut against Fiji at the Hill Dickinson Stadium in Liverpool on 11 July. In his second cap against Argentina a week later, Kloska momentarily packed down with his club teammate, Ellis Genge, who eagle-eyed club statistician Neil Williams says, has become the most-capped international as a Bristol player. with that appearance in Santiago del Estero.

Rugby.title: Richie Mo'unga: 'It's been on my mind, what the comeback would look like'
Rugby.summary: Richie Mo'unga says he's prepared for every scenario as he chases an All Blacks recall after three seasons in Japan.
Rugby.body:
Richie Mo’unga says he’s prepared for every scenario as he chases an All Blacks recall after three seasons in Japan. The 32-year-old will regain national selection eligibility when he runs out off the bench for Canterbury in their season-opening NPC clash with old foes Auckland on Saturday, a highly anticipated return to the selection fold ahead of the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

Having signed an 18-month contract with New Zealand Rugby, Canterbury, and the Crusaders, the 56-Test playmaker says he has one thing on his mind. “Make no mistake, I’m still the same Richie that was here three seasons ago wanting to win every competition I play in,” he told old teammate Israel Dagg on Sport Nation.

Rugby.body:
Scottish Rugby has sacked chief executive Alex Williamson following an independent investigation into his conduct. Williamson began work at Murrayfield in early 2025 after being appointed successor to Mark Dodson the previous September.

Rugby.title: The data shows Dave Rennie's All Blacks can test the all-conquering Springboks to the max
Rugby.summary: The Nations Championship statistics show a drastic change in New Zealand's game plan - one South Africa must work hard to contain.
Rugby.body:
The greatest rivalry in rugby, All Blacks versus Springboks, is the biggest draw the sport has to offer. With the rapid improvement of the All Blacks under new head coach Dave Rennie allied to the crushing weight of history, it could turn out to be the most searching test of Rassie Erasmus’ coaching career to date.

A deep dive into the raw stats produced by the first three rounds of the Nations Championship only whets the appetite for the seven-week tour of the Republic which begins on 7 August, with a game between the Stormers and the visitors in the shadow of Cape Town’s Table Mountain.

Rugby.title: Snyman ready to grasp Springbok challenge after 'hard decision'
Rugby.summary: Andre Snyman revealed he had "no expectation" that his daughter, Keira, would ever wear a Springboks jersey.
Rugby.body:
Andre Snyman revealed he had “no expectation” that his daughter, Keira, would ever wear a Springboks jersey. In July the 38-cap, 10 try former South Africa back watched his 18-year-old daughter represent the Junior Springbok Women for the first time.

By full-time Snyman and her newest teammates had lost 60-17 against a free-flowing USA U20 side, but has taken the first steps to representing the senior Springbok Women. Already her performance has landed her in Cecil Afrika’s Springbok Women’s Sevens training squad. It is not a bad return for a player whose talents were curated at the foot of Colorado’s Rocky Mountains, with her father as coach.

Rugby.title: WRU officially confirm they will axe either Ospreys or Scarlets
Rugby.summary: The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has officially confirmed that Welsh rugby will move to a three-team professional model from the start of the 2028/29 season...
Rugby.body:
The Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has officially confirmed that Welsh rugby will move to a three-team professional model from the start of the 2028/29 season, with either the Ospreys or Scarlets set to effectively be axed.

The WRU announced its future operating model on Wednesday, outlining plans for one professional team in the capital, one in east Wales and one in west Wales. The governing body has already indicated that Cardiff Rugby and Dragons RFC are in line for two of those licences, leaving the Ospreys and Scarlets effectively competing for a single place in west Wales.

Rugby.title: Trailfinders lure 'exciting' England wing to PWR runners-up
Rugby.summary: Two-cap England Red Roses wing Bo Westcombe Evans has joined Trailfinders Women ahead of the 2026/27 Premiership Women's Rugby campaign.
Rugby.body:
Two-cap England Red Roses wing Bo Westcombe Evans has joined Trailfinders Women ahead of the 2026/27 JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby campaign. To date the 24-year-old has spent the entirety of her senior career in the East Midlands with Loughborough Lightning. Last season Westcombe Evans was PWR’s joint-top try-scorer, having crossed the whitewash 12 times in 16 league appearances.

It was Westcombe Evans’ first season back after a year out of rugby with an ACL injury sustained in 2024. The injury occurred just weeks after the wing made her Red Roses debut at the 2024 edition of WXV1 and scored her maiden Test rugby try against the USA Women’s Eagles.

The tourists will be welcomed at a special event at DHL Stadium in Cape Town on Friday before opening their provincial programme against the DHL Stormers at the same venue next week.

Rugby.title: Six England players who could theoretically jump ship to different Test nations
Rugby.summary: World Rugby’s three-year stand-down rule has reshaped international rugby.
Rugby.body:
World Rugby’s three-year stand-down rule has reshaped international rugby. The regulation allows captured players to switch allegiance after 36 months in the Test wilderness, provided they hold the necessary birthright or residency qualifications.

For a handful of former England stars, that window is either wide open or rapidly approaching. The most high-profile name in the rumour mill had been Owen Farrell. The 34-year-old, who won the last of his 112 England caps in the 2023 Rugby World Cup third-place play-off, completes his three-year stand-down this October. But despite his father Andy coaching Ireland, a switch to green is not happening. Farrell does not meet World Rugby’s birthright criteria as his Irish heritage traces back to a great-grandparent, not a parent or grandparent.

Rugby.title: Deep parallels to 2010 for the All Blacks ahead of South Africa
Rugby.summary: It was crisis mode for the All Blacks that triggered an introspective look at the team's tactics, selections and operations. From a kick-heavy game in 2009, they adopted a more expansive, high-risk game.
Rugby.body:
2009 was a great year for South African rugby. It was the year they conquered everyone, from a 2-1 series win in the famous British & Irish Lions tour, to a 3-0 ‘black-wash’ over the All Blacks on the way to a Tri Nations title. After winning the Rugby World Cup in 2007, by 2009 the Boks were sailing high.

The first two Tests at home against New Zealand the boot of Morne Steyn fuelled points while an uncompromising defence and kick pressure choked the All Blacks out of the games.

Rugby.title: Asian Games sevens fixtures confirmed ahead of critical step to Olympics
Rugby.summary: The 2026 Asian Games - the 20th iteration of the sporting event - is set to kick off in Japan in October.
Rugby.body:
The 2026 Asian Games – the 20th iteration of the sporting event – is set to kick off in Japan in October, marking a critical juncture for sevens sides in the region. With the final confirmed list of teams and pools drawn late last week, the Asian Games marks a critical fixture for unions in the region, the event marking a major stop on the way to the Olympics, both for on-field performances and being linked to funding from respective Olympic committees off the field.

The event will form part of a busy two months of sevens action in the region, falling in between two legs of the Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series taking place in the Chinese city of Suzhou (29th-30th August) and Sri Lanka’s largest city, Colombo (17th-18th October).

Rugby.summary: Hawke’s Bay have named a strong side to tackle Wellington in the opening round of New Zealand’s National Provincial Championship.
Rugby.body:
Harry Godfrey may have missed the entire 2026 Super Rugby Pacific season with the Hurricanes due to an ACL injury, but the promising playmaker will get the chance to play at Wellington’s Hnry Stadium this weekend for Hawke’s Bay.

Godfrey sustained the significant injury during a training session with the Magpies last year, which saw the first five-eighth miss the entire title-winning campaign with the Hurricanes. But the 23-year-old is now set for a return, 330 days since last taking the field.

Rugby.summary: Queensland Reds enforcer Lukhan Salakaia-Loto left no stone unturned during a standout Super Rugby Pacific season.
Rugby.body:
Queensland Reds enforcer Lukhan Salakaia-Loto left no stone unturned during a standout Super Rugby Pacific season but still missed out on Wallabies selection. The lock didn’t play in the July Nations Championship Tests, instead finding a silver lining in life away from the rugby field.

Rugby.summary: Lombardy outfit Parabiago won promotion to the top flight for the first time in history when they beat Torino 21-17 in a tense Serie A Championship Grand Final at the end of May.
Rugby.body:
The Federation of Italian Rugby (FIR) have confirmed the structure of its male and female leagues, including the participating teams, with promotion and relegation between the top two divisions restored after a one-year moratorium.

When Colorno withdrew from the 10-team Serie A Elite League at the start of March after running into financial difficulties, their results were expunged and relegation was suspended for the 2025/26 season, leaving the remaining teams safe.

Rugby.summary: The Welsh Rugby Union gives details of how it intends to cut a team - with Ospreys and Scarlets set to fight to be the side in south west Wales.
Rugby.body:
The Welsh Rugby Union has outlined how it plans to cut from four professional teams to three by 2028, with Ospreys and Scarlets set to fight to be the side in south west Wales.

The governing body confirmed in April it intended to press on with plans to go down to three men's teams from the 2028-29 season, with one in the capital, one in the east and one in the west.

Rugby.summary: The Scotland and Lions outside centre, who has won 63 caps for his country, swapped Glasgow for the Côte d'Azur this summer.

Huw Jones admits that joining Toulon is the biggest move of his career, but playing in the Top 14 is an itch that he’s always wanted to scratch since a move to Bayonne fell through.

Rugby.summary: Cheika, who had a three-year spell as Waratahs head coach between 2012 and 2015, is currently working in the NRL.
Rugby.body:
Former Wallabies and Argentina boss Michael Cheika, who has been working in the NRL, could make a sensational return to the NSW Waratahs after a series of targets turned them down.

Cheika had a three-year spell at the helm of the Waratahs between 2012 and 2015 before leaving to take over the Wallabies, and spent last season learning the ropes of coaching in the NRL as an assistant coach at the Sydney Roosters.

Rugby.summary: Aoife Wafer says she will lead with her actions after being named as the new Harlequins captain.
Rugby.body:
Aoife Wafer says she will lead with her actions after being named as the new Harlequins captain. It is the first time the 23-year-old Ireland international has captained a senior team and takes over from Jade Konkel, who retired at the end of last season.

Wafer has captaincy experience, having been a skipper for the youth teams of Leinster and Ireland. Despite her star power making it feel as though the back-row has been on the scene forever, her days in those youth teams ended just five years ago. Taking her first steps as a senior captain for Quins is a “huge honour” for Wafer.

Rugby.title: Joe Schmidt's new role in Irish rugby confirmed
Rugby.summary: The New Zealander left Ireland in 2019, having served as head coach of Leinster and the country's national team.
Rugby.body:
Ulster Rugby have confirmed the appointment of Joe Schmidt as coach development advisor, now that his time with the Wallabies is over. Over the next 12 months, Schmidt will visit Ulster in person and also work remotely to strengthen and develop the coaching pathway across the province.

Schmidt brings a wealth of experience from the highest levels of the game. The New Zealander guided Leinster to two Heineken Cups before leading Ireland to three Six Nations Championships, including a Grand Slam in 2018, and was named World Rugby Coach of the Year the same year.

Rugby.summary: The former Moseley player served as head coach of Estonian men and women, sevens and 15s, and Tallinn Kalev Rugby Club, as well as being Director of Rugby for Estonian Rugby.
Rugby.body:
Coaches always want to leave the organisation they work for in a better place once they move on, and Estonian Rugby will have no complaints on that front when Graham Smith’s time with them officially comes to an end next week.

Smith, a Rugby World Cup-winning coach with England Women in 2014, has spent the last four years in the Baltic country, having been given the all-encompassing task of building the sport up there from pretty much ground zero.

Rugby.summary: The sevens rugby action across the world, with the weekend seeing several regional tournaments produce key results in Asia and Africa.
Rugby.body:
The sevens rugby action across the world, with the weekend seeing several regional tournaments produce key results in Asia and Africa. Starting off in Japan, Nagato Blue Angels won the third round of the Taiyo Seimei Women’s Sevens Series at Mikuni World Stadium in Kitakyushu, blowing away the Mie Pearls 47-0 in the final.

Coming into the tournament as the defending champions, the Blue Angels have also welcomed a strong contingent of international talent in Aussie 7s stars Mackenzie Davis, Amahlia Hala and Kahli Henwood, Fiji’s Ana Naimasi, Chinese Olympian Chen Keyi, and Brazil’s star Bianca Silva.

Rugby.summary: The 2026 Ultimate Sevens coaching staff for the six franchises have been unveiled, ahead of the tournament getting underway in September.
Rugby.body:
The 2026 Ultimate Sevens coaching staff for the six franchises have been unveiled, ahead of the tournament getting underway in September. News has been coming thick and fast for the new sevens tournament, with 16 marquee players and a four round European schedule confirmed earlier this month, with Madrid, Cardiff, Biarritz and London set to host events.

This also came with the announcement of the six franchises – Albion Athletic, Atlantic Novas, Clan Taran, Foudre Bleue, Pacific Current and Sol Feroz – each of whom are set to feature both men’s and women’s teams across the four weekends.

Rugby.title: Rugby World Cups get $90m boost from Australian government, Pacific to benefit
Rugby.summary: Part of Rugby Australia's $90 million World Cup government injection will be spent in the Pacific, breathing life into the code after Moana's controversial Super Rugby exit.
Rugby.body:
Part of Rugby Australia’s $90 million World Cup government injection will be spent in the Pacific, breathing life into the code after Moana’s controversial Super Rugby exit. The package will support the delivery of both next year’s home men’s World Cup and the 2029 women’s showpiece but will also help fund legacy projects focused on the women’s game in Australia and competition in the Pacific.

It follows the Australian government’s $600m investment in the NRL’s Papua New Guinea franchise, set to launch in 2028. Rugby Australia boss Phil Waugh was in Brisbane on Wednesday to spruik the federal government injection ahead of both events.

Rugby.title: Richie Mo'unga named on Canterbury bench for NPC return
Rugby.summary: Returning All Blacks star Richie Mo'unga will be eased back into NPC rugby off the bench as the headliner of the first team namings of the new provincial season.
Rugby.body:
Returning All Blacks star Richie Mo’unga will be eased back into NPC rugby off the bench as the headliner of the first team namings of the new provincial season. Mo’unga’s Canterbury side features All Blacks Sevens flyer-turned-Highlanders playmaker Andrew Knewstubb at No.10, with Chay Fihaki at fullback. Newly capped All Black Jamie Hannah will run out as a starting lock, with breakthrough Blues rookie Torian Barnes named at No.8, and new Canterbury captain Brodie McAlister at hooker. Mo’unga will wear the No.22 jersey in what will be his first game at Christchurch’s new One New Zealand Stadium.

Canterbury will square off with an Auckland team that features Stephen Perofeta as the starting No.10, with capped All Black Angus Ta’avao-Matau also in the run-on side. Ofa Tu’ungafasi is on the bench alongside newly capped Maori All Black Payton Spencer and ex-Wallaby Issak Fines-Leleiwasa.

Rugby.title: Five All Blacks talking points from the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry squad
Rugby.summary: Dave Rennie's 44-man All Blacks squad was unveiled on Monday, and while it featured just three new faces, it inevitably raised plenty more eyebrows.
Rugby.body:
Dave Rennie’s 44-man All Blacks squad was unveiled on Monday, and while it featured just three new faces, it inevitably raised plenty more eyebrows. Du’Plessis Kirifi’s omission was the big talking point for many fans, with the Hurricanes co-captain having just led his team to a historically dominant Super Rugby Pacific final win, just months after wrapping his first season in black. But there is much more to read into with this 44-man list.

What did Rennie prioritise in his selections? Who of the newcomers is best-placed to compete for minutes in the Tests? Will a certain Canterbury first-five get a call-up? Here are five talking points from Monday’s announcement.

Rugby.body:
Sam Cane says he is “stoked” to see ex-teammate Luke Jacobson performing in the black jersey he once wore, sharing high praise for the Chiefs captain as a man who lives up to his ‘Concrete Shoulders’ nickname.

Jacobson’s journey to the All Blacks‘ No.7 jersey has been long, hard-fought, and plagued by injuries. Yet, seven years on from his debut and with just 26 Tests in that span, he has now been rewarded for his patience with three consecutive starts in one of rugby’s most famed shirts.

Wallaroos winger Desiree Miller has been ruled out of the NSW Waratahs’ Super Rugby Champions Final against the Blues, seeing Amelia Whitaker brought in to the run-on side for the clash with the Super Rugby Aupiki winners in Sydney.

The 23-year-old suffered a stress fracture to her right lower leg during the grass-court season and made a late decision to pull out of Wimbledon. Tennis.title: Britain cannot handle Emma Raducanu
Tennis.summary: Britain cannot handle Emma Raducanu The i Paper
Tennis.body:
Once Emma Raducanu had the temerity to win the US Open and thrust herself into the spotlight, it did not take long for her to become a punchbag for armchair sports fans in Britain.

No athlete who is injury prone needs reminding they are injury prone, but in Raducanu’s case there is a gleeful pile-on to ensure she is endlessly aware. The 23-year-old should even just retire, according to some experts in basements, because she would clearly rather pursue various business ventures than focus on tennis.
Tennis.copy:

Tennis.title: 'Most exciting player' Eala shows 'Filipino heart' to make history

Tennis.body:
As the umpire called the winning point, Alexandra Eala collapsed to the ground in tears - knowing her country had been with her for every step of the tournament. She overcame weather delays, and the loss of the first set, to defeat world number three Jessica Pegula in the Washington Open final, becoming the first Filipina to win a WTA title.

"To the Filipino community, here in DC and back home, wherever you are in the world. I really feel all the love." Even Pegula was impressed by the turnout on Monday, for the continuation of Sunday's final.

Tennis.title: Emma Raducanu Pulls Out of US Open
Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu Pulls Out of US Open Tennis Now
Tennis.body:
The 2021 US Open champion is out of Flushing Meadows. Emma Raducanu’s Grand Slam season has taken another painful turn. The 2021 US Open champion has withdrawn from this month’s US Open as she continues recovery from a stress fracture in her right leg, PA Sports reports today.

World No. 49 Raducanu, who reached the Queen’s Club final in June falling to Donna Vekic, was also forced out of Wimbledon due to the injury. “I’ve done everything possible to try to get to the start line but after a final scan tonight the niggle I’ve been managing has developed into a stress fracture,” said Raducanu, who withdrew from Wimbledon the night before The Championships started. “I’ve been medically advised to stop pushing through.”

Tennis.title: Alexandra Eala: Rising Filipina star beats Jessica Pegula in DC Open final to claim first WTA Tour title
Tennis.summary: Alexandra Eala: Rising Filipina star beats Jessica Pegula in DC Open final to claim first WTA Tour title Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Rising Filipina star Alexandra Eala came from a set down against Jessica Pegula to claim the first WTA Tour singles title of her career at the DC Open. Eala had trailed by a set when the match was suspended because of heavy rain on Sunday, but the 21-year-old turned the contest round on Monday to claim a 4-6 6-4 6-0 victory.

The victory made Eala the first Filipina to win a singles title on the tour, completing the same career-defining breakthrough that the Washington tournament once gave Pegula when she claimed her first WTA Tour title in 2019.

Tennis.body:
Serena and Venus Williams have been given a wildcard entry for the women's doubles at the Cincinnati Open. The sisters were scheduled to play together at Wimbledon in July until Serena, 44, picked up a knee injury in her singles comeback loss to Australia's Maya Joint.

The WTA 1000 event which runs from 11-23 August in Ohio will be the first time the siblings have played doubles together since the 2022 US Open. It could also pave the way for Serena to return to play in the US Open this year.

Tennis.title: Eala becomes first Filipino to win WTA singles title
Tennis.summary: Alexandra Eala becomes the first Filipino to win a WTA singles title as she beats top seed Jessica Pegula in a delayed Washington Open final.
Tennis.body:
Alexandra Eala became the first Filipino to win a WTA singles title as she beat top seed Jessica Pegula in a delayed Washington Open final. The WTA showpiece was postponed from Sunday to Monday because of bad weather in the US capital.

Rain and lightning meant the start was pushed back on Sunday, before world number three Pegula took the first set 6-4. Eala, 21, was leading 2-1 in the second set when further bad weather meant play was halted and then cancelled for the rest of the day.

Tennis.title: Emma Raducanu ruled out of US Open
Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu ruled out of US Open The Telegraph
Tennis.body:
Raducanu appears to have developed this stress fracture during her otherwise impressive run to the final of Queen’s in early June. While speaking to reporters at Wimbledon a fortnight later, she described it as “a lower-leg niggle that I’ve been dealing with since … the back end of the clay-court season”.

Without access to medical records, it is difficult to know exactly how Raducanu managed to develop such a serious injury shortly before the biggest tournament of the year. Scans on the eve of Wimbledon were understood to reveal a “grade four” stress fracture, meaning that a line was visible on the MRI scan. After reviewing the evidence, she withdrew from the event at around 10pm the night before it started.

Emma Raducanu will not be playing at the US Open later this month due to an ongoing stress fracture in her lower right leg. It will be the second consecutive major event she has missed after Wimbledon and the last time she played on the Tour was in the final of the HSBC Championships in June.

It is understood that Raducanu’s decision to miss Flushing Meadows was made following a medical consultation. The exact issue she is dealing with is a grade-four stress fracture in her shin. She is currently rehabbing in St Moritz, Switzerland and posted a video of her hitting on a clay court yesterday on Instagram. In the video, she was still wearing a protective boot over the lower part of her leg.

Tennis.summary: Jack Draper explains why he’s been pulling out of tournaments at the very last minute Tennishead
Tennis.body:
Jack Draper is once again preparing for his return to tennis, having not played a competitive match since playing at Eastbourne in July. This run marked the only tournament he has featured in since April, with injuries forcing him to withdraw from the bulk of the clay-court season, including Roland Garros, and then Wimbledon.

It has been a torrid year for the 24-year-old, but he continues to insist that he is close to returning to his peak fitness, although the results are yet to be exhibited. His decision to pull out of Washington drew fresh concerns, but Draper was then awarded a wildcard at the Canadian Open, leaving many confused.

Tennis.title: Jessica Pegula leads Alexandra Eala in rain-affected DC Open final as Kristina Liutova, 16, wins Memphis Classic
Tennis.summary: Jessica Pegula leads Alexandra Eala in rain-affected DC Open final as Kristina Liutova, 16, wins Memphis Classic Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Jessica Pegula holds a one-set lead over Alexandra Eala in a rain-affected DC Open final that saw play suspended until Monday. After severe thunderstorms delayed the initial match start time by three hours, world No 3 Pegula got off to a strong start, taking the first set 6-4 and delighting her home crowd, before rising star Eala took a 2-1 second-set lead against the American.

However, the thunderstorms returned and delayed the resumption of the match for more than five hours, forcing organisers to call play off for the day, with the women's final set to resume at 5pm BST on Monday, before Taylor Fritz faces Rafael Jodar in the men's final no earlier than 6pm, both live on Sky Sports.

Tennis.title: Dog walk and expletive text - key findings in Vondrousova anti-doping case
Tennis.summary: The full report into 2023 Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova's four-year ban for refusing a doping test has been released - BBC Sport analyses the key findings.
Tennis.body:
Recent Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova receiving a four-year ban for refusing to take a doping test was a punishment which sent shockwaves through tennis. The Czech, who became the first unseeded player to win the Wimbledon women's singles title in 2023, would not let a doping control officer into her Prague home to conduct the test in December 2025.

In June, it was announced the 27-year-old would be suspended for four years - the starting point for any player who refuses or evades a test. On Friday, the independent tribunal which imposed the punishment released its full written report about the case - which it described as a "very unfortunate matter" but which offered "no compelling justification" for a shorter ban.

The clamour surrounding this release does not simply come from a brand seeking to make a splash in the market, though. It is the sheer number of players who seem to be uprooting their entire games to pivot that has really caught the eye.

Tennis.body:
Jack Draper has been dealing with on-again, off-again injury issues and has once again withdrawn from a major tournament at the eleventh hour. Most recently, the 24-year-old Brit pulled out of the Mubadala DC Open and Wimbledon just a day before his first match.

Golf.title: Callaway is finally bringing its top Tour iron to retail
Golf.summary: After almost two years of dominating Callaway's Tour staff, the company is finally releasing its latest Apex MB in a limited run. The post Callaway is finally bringing its top Tour iron to retail appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
One of the internet’s most desired Tour-only golf clubs is finally coming to market. Callaway is releasing the Apex MB Tour Raw irons, which are essentially the same irons played by many of Callaway’s top staffers like Sam Burns, Min Woo Lee, Si Woo Kim and more, in “extremely limited quantities.” Apex MB Tour Raw, commonly known on Tour as the Apex MB ’26, is typically Callaway’s most-played iron at PGA Tour events this season.

“We have a saying in the building that great product always finds a way into peoples’ bags,” Callaway’s VP of global strategy, Jacob Davidson, said in a product presentation. “I don’t think there’s a truer testament to that than these irons, because so many players — including non-staffers — have tested them and are currently playing them, despite us keeping supply very limited.

Golf.title: Rules Guy: Is it legal to touch your intended line to remove loose impediments?
Golf.summary: Is it permissible to touch your intended line on the green in order to remove loose impediments? Rules Guy has the answer. The post Rules Guy: Is it legal to touch your intended line to remove loose impediments? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’ve got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. At this year’s Players Championship, Xander Schauffele’s caddie appeared to touch the green on Xander’s line while picking up a loose impediment. What is the rule? —Jim Kelly, Lewisville, NC

Rules 8.2b and 8.1a(2) both mention in that you can’t (a) alter conditions to effect where the ball may go after the next stroke, or (b) move loose impediments to improve the line of play, which seems to restrict the amount of moving of loose impediments you can do. In a scenario where someone wants to putt from a long distance off a green, can they remove all loose impediments along the line all the way to the hole? —Mark McBride, via email

Golf.title: Team Power Rankings: LIV Golf New York
Golf.summary: Team Power Rankings: LIV Golf New York LIV Golf
Golf.body:
Captain Jon Rahm leads Legion XIII into Trump National Golf Club Bedminster, which might prove to be one of the season’s toughest tests. As LIV Golf heads to Trump National Golf Club Bedminster for LIV Golf New York, the stage is set for the 11th stop on the 2026 schedule. It's been nearly three years since the league's last visit to Bedminster, and 33 players from that 2023 field return to a course that has only gotten tougher. The total yardage has been stretched by more than 125 yards, with new back tees adding length to the ninth, 13th and 16th holes.

Trump National Bedminster opened in 2004 under the design of Tom Fazio and has been ranked among the top 100 courses in America by Golf magazine. At 7,651 yards and playing to a par of 71, it's the second-longest course the league has played this season, trailing only Trump National Washington D.C. The course previously hosted LIV Golf events in 2022 and 2023, with Henrik Stenson and 4Aces GC taking the individual and team titles in the first year, and Cameron Smith and Ripper GC sweeping both trophies in the second.

Golf.summary: Our ranking of the year's best majors considers not the fame of the events or their winners or their venues, but their tingly excellence. The post The best major of the year? We ranked all 13 of them (with 1 still to play!) appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The common take these days is that golf’s major season flies by too fast. Here we are, just barely in the grand month of August, one toe in the water, and the season’s long done — that’s how this argument goes. You know: Augusta in April, the PGA in May, Open I in June, Open II in July, majors out.

Well, we’re here to tell you that’s not true — that summation, that whole four-and-done thing, is way too narrow. For starters, there’s one major left, and it’s boffo: the U.S. Amateur (for men), this year at Merion. Come nightfall on Aug. 16, when it wraps and all the shouting is over, maybe the Amateur will get the coveted GOLF.com prize, “Best Major of the Year.” Could happen, but it’s going to have to beat out this amazing threesome of majors to do it, presented here in order of their amazingness. That is, not the fame of the event or its winner or the venue, but the tingly excellence of the event itself.

Golf.body:
Britain's Mimi Rhodes and Leona Maguire, of Ireland, have earned wildcard picks for Europe's Solheim Cup team to take on the United States in the Netherlands next month. Captain Anna Nordqvist has selected Maguire despite missing four cuts in her last six tournaments, including last week's AIG Women's Open at Royal Lytham and St Annes.

The Irishwoman has fallen to 79 in the world but has an impressive record in her three Solheim Cups to date. Rhodes, who will be making her debut, is 92nd in the world rankings and failed to make the weekend in four tournaments in a row before finishing tied 51st at last month's Scottish Open.
