Golf.title: What happens to these players if LIV Golf disappears?
Golf.summary: What happens to these players if LIV Golf disappears? Golfshake.com
Golf.body:
Like rats deserting a sinking ship, many LIV golfers are now looking for somewhere else to play even as they prepare to compete in America this week. And it seems Ian Poulter, Lee Westwood and Graeme McDowell plan to return to the DP World Tour with their tails between their legs. They have all paid their outstanding fines, which represents something of a U-turn. Two years ago Westwood said: "I’m not paying them because I disagree with the way they’ve been handed out."

This is what he says now: "What it does is gives us options having them paid. When the current financial backers of the tour are talking about pulling out and we’re being indemnified, it just makes sense to get them paid straight away before they do pull out. That’s really why we had them paid when we did.

Golf.summary: Michael Thorbjornsen won the 2026 Rocket Classic on Sunday for his first PGA Tour win. Here's a breakdown of what's in his winning golf bag. The post Michael Thorbjornsen’s clubs: Rocket Classic winner has full bag of TaylorMade gear appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Thanks in part to a dramatic 26-foot birdie putt on the 72nd to cap a Sunday 63, Michael Thorbjornsen is now a winner on the PGA Tour, taking the Rocket Classic by two shots. It marks yet another win for TaylorMade’s Spider line of mallet putters — and TaylorMade overall as the former Stanford standout plays a full bag of TM gear. Thorbjornsen stroked the final putt with a Spider Tour X double bend, a putter he switched to earlier this season after beginning his PGA Tour career with a Spider Tour Short Slant.

“You can see how structured his practice is now; the drills, the process,” TaylorMade Tour Rep Adrian Rietveld told GOLF earlier this season during a deep dive of Thorbjornsen’s setup. “He’s gone from a talented putter to more of a student of the game.”

Golf.title: 5 simple keys to help you stop digging your wedges
Golf.summary: Five simple keys that will help you use the bounce of your club more effectively and improve your short game. The post 5 simple keys to help you stop digging your wedges appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
A high, soft pitch is one of the most satisfying shots in golf, and it’s easier to hit than you might think. Start by using a sand wedge or lob wedge. The loft of these clubs helps launch the ball, while the bounce allows the club to glide through the turf.

Many golfers struggle because the leading edge digs into the ground, causing fat or stubbed shots. Learn to use the bounce correctly, and you’ll start hitting crisp, consistent pitch shots around the green.

Golf.title: After Shiho Kuwaki's stunning Women's Open win, 1 unshakeable feeling was everywhere
Golf.summary: Shiho Kuwaki triumphed at Royal Lytham. It was a surprise major victory that will be remembered for everything that could've been. The post After Shiho Kuwaki’s stunning Women’s Open win, 1 unshakeable feeling was everywhere appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Esther Henseleit tapped in for bogey and turned around to look into the fading sunset at Royal Lytham & St Annes. Forty minutes earlier, the 27-year-old German had made the putt of a lifetime, draining a long bomb for birdie on the 72nd hole to tie Shiho Kuwaki and send the AIG Women’s Open to a playoff.

She then missed a much shorter birdie putt to win the first playoff hole and watched as her tee shot on the second playoff hole apparently hit a marshal in the leg and ricocheted into a gorse bush. She hacked out into the fairway, played her third onto the green, but missed her par putt. With Kuwaki in close for par, Henseleit was left to rue a missed opportunity as Kuwaki rolled in the par putt to win the year’s final major in stunning fashion. The 23-year-old from Japan is a multi-time winner on the JLPGA and will be a staple on the LPGA. Make no mistake, Shiho Kuwaki won the AIG Women’s Open. As chaos enveloped Royal Lytham on Sunday, it was Kuwaki who played her final 13 holes in regulation in two under to post five under and put pressure on 54-hole leader Yealimi Noh and Henseleit to match. It was Kuwaki who hit a perfectly flighted iron to the small landing spot on the par-3 ninth for a key birdie. It was Kuwaki who steadied herself after early trouble, played fast and confident, and did what no one else on Sunday could.

Esther Henseleit tapped in for bogey and turned around to look into the fading sunset at Royal Lytham & St Annes. Forty minutes earlier, the 27-year-old German had made the putt of a lifetime, draining a long bomb for birdie on the 72nd hole to tie Shiho Kuwaki and send the AIG Women’s Open to a playoff.

She then missed a much shorter birdie putt to win the first playoff hole and watched as her tee shot on the second playoff hole apparently hit a marshal in the leg and ricocheted into a gorse bush. She hacked out into the fairway, played her third onto the green, but missed her par putt. With Kuwaki in close for par, Henseleit was left to rue a missed opportunity as Kuwaki rolled in the par putt to win the year’s final major in stunning fashion. The 23-year-old from Japan is a multi-time winner on the JLPGA and will be a staple on the LPGA. Make no mistake, Shiho Kuwaki won the AIG Women’s Open. As chaos enveloped Royal Lytham on Sunday, it was Kuwaki who played her final 13 holes in regulation in two under to post five under and put pressure on 54-hole leader Yealimi Noh and Henseleit to match. It was Kuwaki who hit a perfectly flighted iron to the small landing spot on the par-3 ninth for a key birdie. It was Kuwaki who steadied herself after early trouble, played fast and confident, and did what no one else on Sunday could.

Golf.title: Yealimi Noh suffered Women's Open heartbreak — but found what she'd been missing
Golf.summary: Yealimi Noh watched her AIG Women's Open dreams slip away on Sunday, but she left Royal Lytham with something she'd been missing. The post Yealimi Noh suffered Women’s Open heartbreak — but found what she’d been missing appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Yealimi Noh had envisioned herself winning the AIG Women’s Open. As all talented pros do, Yealimi Noh had drawn herself in the stars before she even started to climb the pro golf ladder.

But she arrived at this year’s AIG Women’s Open “unsure” about her game. After a brutal season that saw her go six events without breaking par in a single round, the 25-year-old Noh found herself no longer enjoying golf as she once did. Golf had always been a “job,” but it was different when the game no longer loved you back. When your hard work isn’t being rewarded and when the course only brings you stress and hurt. After missing back-to-back cuts at the KPMG Women’s PGA Championship and Amundi Evian Championship, Yealimi Noh found herself lost, adrift as she looked to rediscover her world-class game and the motivation to hone it.

Golf.body:
If you’ve heard of SWAG Golf, you may have heard of the 45-second sellouts, the one-of-one special search for headcovers, or the exclusive groups where SWAG fans buy sell and trade their gear in hopes of creating the ultimate collection. If you’ve followed the brand over the past few years, you have started to see them transition to more in-stock product and a wider catalog of products to get more SWAG into more hands. Recently they introduced the ‘SWAG Essentials’ collection, so let’s take a look at their new lineup of in-stock accessories.

The SWAG Golf Essentials Shoe Bag is made from a polyester/vinyl style material that’s durable and water-resistant while providing ventilation so there’s no stinky shoe problems on the drive home from the course. I also think it’s the perfect size. It’s large enough that it’s easy to get shoes in an out of the bag without any problems, but it’s streamlined enough to not be a pain to travel with. I’ve actually been using it even when I’m flying. I just throw my shoes in the bag and then throw the bag in my travel bag with no issues.

Have you ever had a day when you just didn’t feel like going to work? It can happen to anyone. Even someone whose job is playing golf. Forgive Davis Riley, but 2026 has been that kind of season.

Golf.summary: England's Lottie Woad and Charley Hull are both in contention going into the final round of the AIG Women's Open at Royal Lytham and St Annes.
Golf.body:
England's Lottie Woad and Charley Hull are both in contention heading into the final round of the AIG Women's Open at Royal Lytham and St Annes. Woad carded a one-under 70 on Saturday to sit at three under while Hull recovered from three early bogeys to sign for a 71, leaving herself five shots behind leader Yealimi Noh, at two under overall.

"I was pretty proud," Hull told Sky Sports. The 30-year-old, who is chasing her maiden major title after being a runner-up on five occasions, crucially made birdies on the 15th and 16th holes as she fought back on the back nine and then scrambled to save par on the penultimate hole.

After six holes on Saturday, Haeran Ryu’s march to history seemed destined. Gunning for her third consecutive major win, Ryu had birdied three of her first six holes to stretch her lead to four at the AIG Women’s Open.

A coronation appeared to be in the cards. Chaos arrived instead. Ryu blew her tee shot on the par-5 seventh into a thick gorse bush and had to take an unplayable. She made bogey and dropped another shot at No. 8. Bogeys at 10, 12 and 14 came like haymakers as Ryu went from up four to trailing by three as the wind and brutal back nine at Royal Lytham and St. Annes refused to let her off the mat.

Golf.title: ‘Hey, buddy, come with me’: Pro’s hole in one comes with a surprise
Golf.summary: Matt Kuchar’s hole in one during the second round of the Rocket Classic at Detroit Golf Club came with a surprise. The post ‘Hey, buddy, come with me’: Pro’s hole in one comes with a surprise appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Matt Kuchar made a hole in one, then, very possibly, a fan for life. The former came Friday afternoon on the 163-yard, par-3 5th hole at Detroit Golf Club. Struck by a 9-iron, Kuchar’s ball touched down about 30 feet short of the hole, bounced a few times and rolled before curling over the cup’s right side on its last rotation. Kuchar hadn’t seen the result, though. He’d grabbed his peg and was walking off the tee box when he learned what had happened during the Rocket Classic’s second round.

“If I hit a full 9-iron and put a little draw on it, which came out perfectly, I thought it would be a good shot,” he said. “It was tracking very nicely and it looked like the ball stopped from my perspective. Golf.title: At American Century Championship, there was gold medal karaoke
Golf.summary: The American Century Championship was filled with the normal celebrity high jinks, but two gold medal stars stole the show at karaoke. The post At American Century Championship, there was gold medal karaoke appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The American Century Championship at Lake Tahoe is always filled with celebrity high jinks, and this year’s edition was no different. Brothers Brady and Matthew Tkachuk, two stars of the United States’ gold-medal-winning hockey team, were in the field along with Matthew Boldy. Former U.S. Men’s National Team forward and current MLS announcer Taylor Twellman was also at Lake Tahoe and joined the latest edition of GOLF’s Subpar podcast with Colt Knost and Drew Stoltz to detail the event and discuss the World Cup.

Mardy Fish won the tournament, but the Tkachuk brothers stole the show at karaoke, according to Twellman. “The Tkachucks killed it,” Twellman told Knost and Stoltz. “Dream On was a no-brainer. But the best part was that they did not know that they had to sing the next night. So Matt and Brady were like, ‘Hold on, we’ve got to do this again?’ No voices. Obviously, they’ve been going at it for a couple of nights. So the second rendition may not have been as good as the first one. But listen, Boldy marked his ball with his gold medal.

Golf.title: Tony Finau's 'low season' has had lessons and 1 rare occurrence
Golf.summary: Tony Finau has struggled in 2026. That season came with a rare occurrence and a lot of lessons that he's using to fight to make the playoffs. The post Tony Finau’s ‘low season’ has had lessons and 1 rare occurrence appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
It has been a season to forget for Tony Finau. The six-time PGA Tour winner has made 14 of 20 cuts this year, but has just one top 10. He hasn’t been in the mix on the weekend since the CJ Cup Byron Nelson in May. After missing the cut at the 3M Open, Finau arrived at this week’s Rocket Classic, an event he won in 2022, sitting at 87 in the FedEx Cup Playoffs standings and needing to do some work over the final two weeks to secure his postseason bid.

“I don’t know if pressure’s the right word, more than I haven’t been happy with the results, I haven’t played the way I know I can play,” Finau said on Friday at the Rocket Classic. “For whatever reason it’s been a low season for me, but I continue to stay enthusiastic about each week and the future. I feel like my future’s still bright even on a season like this.”

Golf.title: How many wedges should you carry? Ask yourself these questions
Golf.summary: How should you decide what number of wedges to carry? True Spec's Matt Morin shares the questions you should ask yourself to find out. The post How many wedges should you carry? Ask yourself these questions appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
According to the Rules of Golf, the maximum number of clubs you can carry in a given round is 14. But the set makeup is totally up to you. Maybe you’re a long bomber and choose to carry a number of wedge lofts at the bottom of your bag. Or maybe you’re a shorter hitter, and prefer to load up on the top end with hybrids and fairway woods instead.

A “standard” set of 14 clubs generally consists of a driver, two fairway woods, one or two hybrids, five or six irons, three wedges (Gap, PW, SW) and a putter. But of course, there are endless variations which are entirely dependent on a player’s preferences. Still, many players are curious about how many wedges they should have in their bag — especially when it comes to carrying a scoring club like a lob wedge. What’s a perplexed player to do? I asked True Spec VP of Sales Matt Morin for his take.

Golf.title: Callaway's new Quantum Mini Spinner has my head spinning
Golf.summary: Callaway's new Quantum Mini Spinner is a 'mini revolution' for its category. Here's why it might end up in your bag too. The post Callaway’s new Quantum Mini Spinner has my head spinning appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I am not a fan of high-lofted fairway woods for a large bucket of players. I think the popularity growth on the PGA Tour created a misunderstanding of what high-lofted fairway woods are supposed to do and mean to a player, and I’ve not been shy about my stance. There’s nothing inherently wrong with them, but it’s also the club I see more in the garages of my golf buddies than in their bags.

But Callaway may have just completely flipped me to the dark side with their new Quantum Mini Spinner — even though it was by no means designed for a player like me. I got the chance to test out the Mini Spinner a while ago at the Callaway ambassador shoot with Johnny Thompson and at the time I wasn’t really sold. To be honest, it was mostly because I didn’t want to be sold. It was just a quick demo to see the product and get an understanding for what they were trying to do with it, but it just didn’t seem like something I wanted to care about. Why would I want a fairway wood that spun more? The spin was already the thing I hated most about high-lofted fairway woods. I can’t flight them down, and they are useless into the wind. I play most of my golf outside of Chicago so that’s a major factor in my club choice. I had ignored the club until we arrived at Callaway’s ECPC in Carlsbad, Cali. where a built-to-spec Quantum Mini Spinner 7W was waiting for me on the range.

Golf.summary: LIV Golf Is On The Cusp Of A New Funding Deal—And Bankruptcy Is On The Table Forbes
Golf.body:
The embattled LIV Golf league is well on its way to a deal worth between $250 million and $350 million that would save it from what once looked like an inevitable folding after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund backed away from its promise to support the league through 2032.

CEO Scott O’Neil, who joined the league last year, is close to completing a deal that will support the league through at least 2027 and fund the creation of “LIV 2.0,” a scaled-down version of the league, a source familiar with talks told Forbes on Friday.

Golf.title: Head-to-head: Herbert’s 2026 UK dominance vs. DeChambeau’s 2023 Greenbrier magic

Golf.body:

There have been four in the league’s first 56 regular-season tournaments. In addition, there is the record seven-shot win by Cameron Smith three years ago at Bedminster, site of next week’s LIV Golf New York tournament.

Of those huge wins, two stand apart from the rest - Bryson DeChambeau's demolition at The Greenbrier in 2023 and Lucas Herbert's record-breaking week at LIV Golf United Kingdom presented by JCB last week. Different formats, different courses, three years apart, but the two performances invite a natural comparison as arguably the most dominant individual showings the league has produced.

Golf.title: Hull responds to criticism of prank on caddie
Golf.summary: Golfer Charley Hull tells critics to "lighten up" after receiving backlash for a scratchcard prank she played on her caddie.
Golf.body:
Golfer Charley Hull has told critics to "lighten up" after receiving backlash for a scratchcard prank she played on her caddie. In the lead up to the ongoing Women's Open at Royal Lytham & St Annes, Hull revealed she had purchased the ticket in a Blackpool joke shop and used it to trick caddie Adam Woodward into believing he had won £100,000 – a moment she caught on camera.

While many people have seen the funny side of the incident, Hull has faced criticism both on social media and from figures within golf, including four-time major winner Dame Laura Davies, who described the stunt as "extremely cruel" when asked about it on commentary.

Golf.title: How a simple golf travel hack saved me a nasty baggage fee
Golf.summary: One of the benefits of a traveling life in golf is painful experience. This travel hack came from an epic failure ... and saved me another. The post How a simple golf travel hack saved me a nasty baggage fee appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Some lessons need to be learned the hard way. And some lessons need to be learned the hardest way. Learning that the stove is hot? That’s a lesson learned the hard way. Learning that it’s better to test the temperature of the pool before jumping in? Hard way. Learning that the golf course will give away your tee time if you show up late? Hard way.

But learning the baggage weight limits of a certain transatlantic airline are firm and unyielding — even for frequent fliers, and even for oversized baggage — in front of an increasingly impatient baggage line of a few-hundred people in terminal 2 of Paris’ Charles de Gaulle airport? That, my friends, is a lesson learned the hardest way.

Golf.body:
The most terrifying sound in golf is silence—the quiet that falls when you stand over your ball with all eyes on you. The absence of noise can unsettle even seasoned players. And nowhere does it ring out louder than on the 1st tee of the East Course at Merion Golf Club.

On the scorecard, the par-4 opener is a friendly handshake. At 358 yards, it can be tackled with a long iron and a wedge. But consider the location of the tee box, directly alongside the clubhouse terrace, where glasses clink and silverware clatters amid the buzz of conversation. That is, until someone steps up to hit.

Golf.title: Report: LIV Golf close to securing investment to support league’s future
Golf.summary: Report: LIV Golf close to securing investment to support league’s future Sports Business Journal
Golf.body: LIV Golf has “received ‘multiple written commitments from blue-chip investment firms that would serve as anchor investors to support the league’ going forward,” according to sources cited by Mark Cannizzaro of the N.Y. POST. LIV Golf CEO Scott O’Neil is “believed to have been seeking between” $250M-$300M. The prospective investors “have submitted qualified term sheets” that would “support the formation of a financing syndicate with sufficient backing to capitalize” what LIV Golf is calling “LIV 2.0.” Sources added that LIV has “also attracted interest from additional investors looking to participate alongside those anchor investors.” There are “believed to be some high-level meetings scheduled to take place next week” at the LIV event at Trump Bedminster in N.J., meetings that will include O’Neil and LIV players. The sources said that the “expectation is that a deal will be finalized ‘sometime in September.’” But it is unclear how LIV will look in 2027 as it moves forward. There has been “talk of a heavier emphasis on team golf, but that remains to be seen.” Under the proposed structure outlined in the term sheet, LIV players will “own a majority stake in the league” (N.Y. POST, 7/29).

LIV remains in trouble despite reports the breakaway tour has found a lifeline to keep afloat in 2027, according to golf reporter Dan Rapaport. The breakaway tour, which launched in 2022 after luring multiple PGA Tour winners, major champions and ageing European Ryder Cup stars with gargantuan contracts and $25m prize purses, has been in peril ever since Saudi Arabia announced it will withdraw its financial backing at the end of the season.

The seismic announcement left their chief executive, Scott O'Neil, in a race against time to secure funding from new investors to keep the league afloat in 2027. O'Neil previously revealed LIV needed between $300-350m and had to secure the cash by the beginning of September to plan accordingly for next season.

Golf.summary: Wondering if a mini driver would be a good fit for your game? True Spec's Matt Morin explains the popular club's benefits. The post Mini driver vs. 3-wood: Which one belongs in your bag? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
You’ve likely been hearing a lot about mini drivers — a club category that exists in between regular drivers and 3-woods. What is a mini driver exactly? Mini drivers generally have stronger lofts than 3-woods but weaker lofts than drivers. They also have smaller heads and shorter shaft lengths than standard drivers, which makes them more forgiving and easier to hit off the tee.

“Mini drivers have taken the world by storm over the last couple of years,” said True Spec VP of sales Matt Morin. “With the game of golf evolving, we have also seen a ‘turn-back-in-time’ movement. The traditional driver’s head size and shape from the early 2000s were always the smaller profile that allowed the better player to be able to utilize the club off the fairway and the tee. The mini driver profile has become smaller than your traditional driver head shape but bigger than your modern 3-wood, which allows for more forgiveness on tee shots that do not call for the driver.”

Golf.body:
Former PGA Tour winner Trey Mullinax was hit with a six-month PGA Tour suspension on Wednesday for violating the Tour’s Anti-Doping Policy. Mullinax, who has one PGA Tour win and two Korn Ferry Tour wins over his career, tested positive for a banned substance, for which he took full responsibility but denied trying to gain a “competitive advantage” in a statement on Wednesday.

The PGA Tour released a concurrent statement that failed to provide many details. Late afternoon on Wednesday, the Tour released its statement about Mullinax, in which they said Mullinax had violated the Tour’s ban on “performance-enhancing substances” by testing positive for a prohibited substance.

Golf.title: This simple fix had me reading greens like a pro | The Lab
Golf.summary: I entered my putting lesson with Stephen Sweeney thinking I was a terrible green-reader. I left ready to take on the world. Here's how. The post This simple fix had me reading greens like a pro | The Lab appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
We’re now on Episode 3 of The Lab with PGA Tour Putting Performance Advisor Stephen Sweeney, and I’ve not been shy about how this experience changed my game. In Episode 1 we talked all about setup, and Sweeney basically changed every single part of how my body sets up to the ball. In Episode 2 he walked me through the idea of capture speed, and how staying consistent with your intended speed can help make more putts, and now for Episode 3 we’re tackling green reading. I wasn’t shy about green reading being the worst part of my putting performance, but one simple sentence ended up turning it all around.

As we know from previous episodes there’s basically three reasons a player will miss a putt. There are technical reasons, which include a small portion of the actual equipment in your hands, there’s speed control, and there’s the read you decided on in the first place. As Sweeney explains in the video, the majority of the time the problem starts with the read the player thought they had in their head.

Golf.title: I never walk without my Motocaddy. Here's how they just made it better | I Tried It
Golf.summary: The 2026 Motocaddy M7 Remote makes the walk easier for players who need a bit more help to finish the round. The post I never walk without my Motocaddy. Here’s how they just made it better | I Tried It appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I’ve had a Motocaddy Electric Caddy for three years now, dating back to the 2024 model of the M7 Remote GPS. For me, the Motocaddy unlocked a whole new world. I have some sports injuries from the past that are quite troublesome when walking 18 holes while carrying a bag or even pushing a cart, but the Motocaddy freed up the stress on my joints to enjoy my rounds with friends who also enjoy the walk. Last year I upgraded to the 2025 model of the M7 Remote, and for the past two months I have been using the 2026 model of the M7 Remote.

So how does Motocaddy continue to make the product better every year? Let’s dive in. The Motocaddy M7 Remote (2026) is a three-wheeled electric caddy that you can steer around the golf course with a remote. They also have a cheaper M5 model without the remote as well as a more expensive M7 Remote GPS which unlocks the ability for the on-board screen to act as a course GPS; you can plot out distance to hazards and yardages to the front, middle and back of greens. You can also pair their caddies with one of their golf bags, which feature their unique locking system. That saves you from having to strap in the bottom of the bag and makes getting the clubs on the trolley faster and more secure. I like the EliteFlex Hybrid Golf Bag.

Golf.title: The LPGA's dream is in sight. But Charley Hull must achieve hers first
Golf.summary: At the AIG Women's Open, the LPGA's dream can be seen on the horizon. But Charley Hull must achieve her own dream first. The post The LPGA’s dream is in sight. But Charley Hull must achieve hers first appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Late NBA commissioner David Stern called it a “blessing.” When Stern took over the NBA in 1984, the league was in hard times, fighting to gain a foothold on national television and trying to stabilize itself. While it was Stern’s ambition and innovative business sense that were credited with propelling the NBA into its global future, that would not have been possible without two key figures: Bird and Magic. What Stern understood was that, to capture attention and demand eyeballs, star power — and rivalries more specifically — sells.

In Larry Bird and Magic Johnson, Stern had two stars: one a stoic trash-talker and the other a charismatic competitor. That the two had already locked horns in college was a bonus. Stern directed the NBA’s marketing arm to lean into the individual rivalry, to promote games as Bird and the Celtics or Magic’s Lakers instead of, simply, Lakers vs. Celtics. That decision and the subsequent arrival of Michael Jordan took the NBA from a down-on-its-luck, tape-delay league to the superpower it is today. Twenty years after a rivalry transformed the NBA, professional golf found its own transformation courtesy of Tiger Woods. Woods’ transcendent talent was enough to reshape the conversation around pro golf itself, but adding Phil Mickelson, a diametric rival, helped usher in a whole new audience to the PGA Tour as fans flocked to see if Woods, the robotic killer, could make history and whether the risky and charismatic Mickelson could be a proper foil to greatness.

Following the safe arrival of her baby son, the next biggest date in Georgia Hall's diary comes this week as she returns to the scene of her greatest golfing triumph. Aged just 22 and with her dad Wayne caddying, Hall won the 2018 AIG Women's Open in great style at Royal Lytham and St Annes. She remains the most recent British female player to win a major.

Now Hall, 30, is back on the Fylde coast, with five-month-old son Conor and the rest of her family in tow. It was only when she first picked up a club again six weeks after giving birth that she entertained the idea of coming back to the venue that means so much to her.

Golf.title: 'It's sad to see': Rising star laments loss of this week's PGA Tour event

Golf.body:
The 2026 edition of the Rocket Classic has a lot going for it. It has a newly renovated, Donald Ross-designed host course in Detroit Golf Club. It has a star-studded field featuring top pros like Cameron Young and Xander Schauffele. And the tournament has a defending champion, Aldrich Potgieter, who is among the most talented young stars around.

Unfortunately, this week’s event will likely be the last Rocket Classic ever. Between the title sponsor’s departure from the tournament and the PGA Tour’s impending schedule overhaul, the beloved event is off the schedule next season, and the chances of it making the cut for the PGA Tour’s new top tier in 2028 and beyond are low.

Golf.title: Poulter Revives Union Jack Trousers 22 Years On at LIV Golf UK
Golf.summary: Poulter Revives Union Jack Trousers 22 Years On at LIV Golf UK golfpost.com
Golf.body:
Twenty-two years after one of professional golf's most memorable fashion moments, Ian Poulter walked onto the final round of LIV Golf UK on July 26 wearing his iconic Union Jack trousers — and delivered his strongest performance of the 2026 season in front of a home crowd at Rocester, England.

The flag-print design was a direct echo of his appearance at the 133rd Open Championship at Royal Troon on July 15, 2004, where Poulter wore the same ensemble, challenging professional golf's strict dress codes and establishing his reputation as the sport's most daring dresser. The look at Royal Troon — where he tied for 25th place — became one of the most celebrated fashion moments in golf history and inspired his IJP clothing line. FOX Sports documented the outfit during final-round coverage at JCB Golf & Country Club, where the scenes drew an unmistakable line back to that defining day two decades ago.

Golf.title: Tiger and Phil vanished from this major season. But at Lytham, history lingers
Golf.summary: Tiger and Phil’s absence looms over the end of major season. So too does Annika’s Grand Slam victory at Lytham, host of this Women’s Open. The post Tiger and Phil vanished from this major season. But at Lytham, history lingers appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Women’s Open Championship is being held this week at Royal Lytham, where Annika Sorenstam completed her career grand slam in 2003. A few months earlier, she had played in a PGA Tour event, at Colonial. Interest in Annika, 23 summers ago, was high, intensely so, and her golf, like her personality and her language, was memorably precise.

I was once following her in a tournament round during this time period and heard Annika ask a playing partner to mark her ball on the green before Annika played a shot—from 130 or more yards out. After the round, I told Annika that I had never heard a player make such a request, not from that distance. “You should watch me play more golf,” Annika said in her no-nonsense way. Ah-nee-KAH. I often wondered how she would adapt to life in Florida—she was so Swedish. Nelly Korda, a child of European parents herself and the reigning U.S. Open winner, has a great opportunity this week to make her own linksland mark on the game, by winning her first Open Championship in the very place where Annika won hers.

Golf.title: 5 keys to help you unlock more speed and master the high bomb
Golf.summary: Want more distance off the tee? Learn to hit a high, towering drive with these five simple keys from a Top 100 Teacher. The post 5 keys to help you unlock more speed and master the high bomb appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Every golfer knows the feeling. You step onto a tee box with a wide-open fairway and only one thing on your mind: “Time to let the big dog eat.” Unfortunately, that’s usually when things go sideways.

Instead of creating more speed, most golfers try to manufacture it — swinging harder, tensing up and throwing their sequence out of sync. Ironically, the harder they chase distance, the less of it they find.

Golf.title: The new Arccos app takes a big step forward to help golfers improve
Golf.summary: Arccos Golf has always been great at giving players the "what" and the "why," but the new app update offers something more. The post The new Arccos app takes a big step forward to help golfers improve appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I’ve now been using Arccos for about four months, and it truly has changed the way that I look at my game. About a month ago, they launched an update to their app, and everything I thought I learned suddenly had a different perspective. Arccos has always explored the “what” in your game; some may even say it’s covered the “why.” But now it’s exploring the “how”.

Let’s dive into the new Arccos app update. The app has expanded. There’s now more information available, more swipes to be had, and more reason than ever to spend time in the app after your round. The new software update has also improved the accuracy of all of their algorithms, including the features integrated with Arccos Air and the Arccos Smart Laser.

Golf.title: Don't make this common mistake when practicing your golf swing
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Kevin Sprecher explains the right — and wrong — ways to practice your golf swing on the range. The post Don’t make this common mistake when practicing your golf swing appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When golfers practice, most become overly focused on hitting the ball. They may start with the intention of working on a swing change, but as soon as the ball is placed in front of them, their attention shifts to making contact and producing a “good” shot.

The result is usually the same familiar swing. When you are working on your mechanics, the goal should not be to hit the ball. Instead, the goal is to make the new swing and observe how that motion affects the ball. The ball provides feedback, but it should not control the movement.

Golf.body:
When the PGA Tour descended upon the Travelers Championship in June to announce major changes to the future of professional golf, at least some in the golf world rolled their eyes.

The changes as outlined by the Tour had been in the works for months … and expected by many inside the sport’s orbit for roughly as long. The real excitement wasn’t going to be laid out in a carefully choreographed press conference, it was going to be scrapped, clawed and cudgeled over in the back rooms and board meetings where golf’s business really gets done. In other words, it was going to be up to the sponsors.

Badminton.title: Badminton: Indonesian pairs withdraw from worlds amid match-fixing probe
Badminton.summary: Badminton: Indonesian pairs withdraw from worlds amid match-fixing probe The Star
Badminton.body:
PETALING JAYA: Indonesia’s world No. 13 mixed doubles pair Jafar Hidayatullah-Felisha Pasaribu have come under the spotlight following an alleged match-fixing investigation involving several Indonesian players.

Although there has been no official confirmation linking the pair to the case, their withdrawal from the tournament has fuelled speculation. The Indonesian Badminton Association (PBSI) secretary-general Ricky Soebagdja said in a statement that Jafar-Felisha, as well as another mixed doubles pair, Adnan Maulana-Indah Cahya Sari Jamil, had been withdrawn as part of adjustments to Indonesia’s squad for the World Championships.

Badminton.title: Indonesia drop two mixed doubles pairs BWF over match-fixing probe
Badminton.summary: Indonesia drop two mixed doubles pairs BWF over match-fixing probe NST Online
Badminton.body:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Indonesia Badminton Association (PBSI) has withdrawn two mixed doubles pairs from the World Championships on Aug 17-23 in New Delhi, following the ongoing match-fixing investigations being conducted by the Badminton World Federation (BWF).

The two pairs implicated are world No. 13 Jafar Hidayatullah-Felisha Pasaribu and world No. 24 Adnan Maulana-Indah Cahya Sari Jamil. "This decision is part of the organisation's efforts to ensure that all administrative processes and athlete participation in international championships are carried out in accordance with the applicable regulations and procedures," said PBSI in a statement on Tuesday.

Badminton.title: Tanvi Sharma announces her arrival with first BWF World Tour title, becomes youngest winner in tournament's history | Hindustan Times
Badminton.summary: Tanvi Sharma announces her arrival with first BWF World Tour title, becomes youngest winner in tournament's history | Hindustan Times hindustantimes.com
Badminton.body:
The teenager won the final in straight games in Chinese Taipei, making amends after losing three previous finals. NEW DELHI: Tanvi Sharma has announced her arrival. All the talk about the young shuttler’s talent and skill was on display as she won her maiden BWF World Tour title at the $250,000 Taipei Open on Sunday.

Just 17, Tanvi captured the title after delivering a masterclass against Vietnamese Nguyen Thuy Linh, beating the sixth seed 21-16, 21-16 in 36 minutes at the Taipei Arena. The shuttler from Punjab also cemented her legacy as the youngest winner across any discipline in the tournament’s 46-year history.

Badminton.title: Taipei Open: Blissfully Unaware, Unmistakably Historic
Badminton.summary: Taipei Open: Blissfully Unaware, Unmistakably Historic BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
The record came as news to Tanvi Sharma. Fresh off the biggest victory of her young career, the 17-year-old Indian was told she had become the youngest champion in Taipei Open history, eclipsing the mark set by her idol, Tai Tzu Ying. Her first response was one of genuine surprise.

“Really? I wasn’t aware of that,” Sharma said with a smile. “It’s such an honour. Tai is my idol. I’m really, really happy to win this title.” By then, however, history had already been written.

Badminton.title: 17-year-old Tanvi Sharma clinches maiden BWF World Tour title with Taipei Open win
Badminton.summary: 17-year-old Tanvi Sharma clinches maiden BWF World Tour title with Taipei Open win wionews.com
Badminton.body:
Seventeen-year-old Tanvi Sharma won her maiden BWF World Tour Super 300 title and created history by becoming the youngest player, across all categories, to win the Taipei Open. Tanvi defeated Vietnam’s sixth-seeded Nguyen Thuy Linh 21-16, 21-16 in the women’s singles final on Sunday (Aug 2). With this victory, she became only the second Indian women’s singles player to claim the title after Saina Nehwal, who won the tournament in 2008, ending India’s 17-year wait for a crown at the event. It was India’s third overall title at the Taipei Open, following Jwala Gutta and V Diju’s mixed doubles triumph in 2009, when the tournament was part of the Grand Prix Gold circuit.

Tanvi made a strong start in the opening game, taking a 10-2 lead. Nguyen fought back to reduce the deficit to 10-8, but Tanvi remained in control and closed out the game 21-16.

Badminton.title: Teen Sensation Tanvi Sharma Scripts History, Wins Taipei Open for Maiden BWF World Tour Title
Badminton.summary: Teen Sensation Tanvi Sharma Scripts History, Wins Taipei Open for Maiden BWF World Tour Title Open Magazine
Badminton.body:
Seventeen-year-old Tanvi Sharma announced herself on the global badminton stage in emphatic fashion on Sunday, defeating Vietnam's sixth seed Nguyen Thuy Linh in straight games to lift the Taipei Open Super 300 title and claim the first BWF World Tour crown of her career.

The Indian prodigy needed just 36 minutes to outclass the experienced Vietnamese 21-16, 21-16, capping a breakthrough week with one of the biggest wins of her young career. The triumph also earned Tanvi a place in the record books. At 17 years and 222 days, she became the youngest champion in the history of the Taipei Open and only the fourth Indian women's singles player to win a BWF Super 300-or-higher title.

Badminton.summary: Tanvi Sharma wins Taipei Open 2026 title, beats Nguyen Thuy Linh for maiden BWF World Tour crown Sportstar
Badminton.body:
Tanvi Sharma beat Nguyen Thuy Linh to win the Taipei Open 2026 BWF Super 300 on Sunday, marking her maiden World Tour title. The 17-year-old maintained a comfortable lead over World No. 21 to win straight games 21-16, 21-16 and bag the victory in just 36 minutes, becoming the first women’s singles victor here since Saina Nehwal in 2008.

Tanvi had previously beaten Nguyen at the opening round of the 2025 US Open. In the contest, she played Nguyen strategically, with clean cross-court shots that made her opponent, who was already showing signs of fatigue by the second game, run around the court.

Tanvi had previously beaten Nguyen at the opening round of the 2025 US Open. In the contest, she played Nguyen strategically, with clean cross-court shots that made her opponent, who was already showing signs of fatigue by the second game, run around the court.

Badminton.title: Beyond junior glory | Ayush Shetty @ 2026 BWF World Championships
Badminton.summary: Beyond junior glory | Ayush Shetty @ 2026 BWF World Championships India Today
Badminton.body:
For Ayush Shetty, his badminton journey didn’t begin in a training academy but in his backyard in Sanoor, Karnataka. At the age of eight, he was introduced to the sport by his father. “As I gained interest and started to enjoy the game, my family decided to move to Bengaluru so that I could get better training,” says Ayush.

It was the family sacrifice that transformed a young dreamer into one of India’s brightest badminton stars. Ayush made his mark on the international stage by winning a bronze at the 2023 BWF World Junior Championships. His rise to the senior circuit has been equally remarkable. In 2025, the 21-year-old won his maiden BWF World Tour title at the US Open Super 300 and became the first Indian men’s singles player since 1965 to reach the Badminton Asia Championships final. He had displayed a rigorous training mindset.

Ranked 67th in the world – 56 places below their experienced opponents – the Malaysians displayed remarkable composure to recover from the disappointment of letting a game point slip at 20-19 in the opener before taking charge of the next two.

Completing the career Grand Slam, she secured the Badminton Asia Championships title in 2026, establishing herself as one of the most accomplished players of her generation.

Badminton.title: Taipei Open: Cheers Carry Lee Through
Badminton.summary: Taipei Open: Cheers Carry Lee Through BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
For 70 exhausting minutes, Lee Chia Hao slogged against Riki Takei, refusing to let an opportunity to regain his confidence slip away. Roared on by a passionate crowd, the Chinese Taipei men’s singles player survived a tense opening-round battle, sealing a 21-15 14-21 25-23 victory after seeing four consecutive match points erased.

Lee admitted he drew strength from the fans who had waited a year to see him compete at home. “It’s been a long time since I played here,” Lee said. “It feels different from playing abroad. Being on home ground, with so many fans cheering me on, makes me feel even more excited and gives me a greater sense of drive.”

Badminton.body:
Mixed doubles defending champions Chen Tang Jie and Toh Ee Wei have withdrawn from the BWF World Championships 2026 due to Toh’s ongoing recovery from a major knee injury. Toh had suffered an Anterior Crucial Ligament (ACL) injury in her left knee during their quarterfinals match at the KFF Singapore Open 2026 in May. Following surgery, the world No.7 is undergoing rehabilitation.

Malaysia will still have two pairs among the mixed doubles qualifiers, as the next eligible pair in the reserves list were Wong Tien Ci/Lim Chiew Sien, who will join senior compatriots Goh Soon Huat/Shevon Lai Jemie in the draw.

Competitor News.title: Revolut becomes Front-of-Shirt sponsor of Serie A club Como 1907
Competitor News.summary: Revolut becomes Front-of-Shirt sponsor of Serie A club Como 1907 FX News Group
Competitor News.body:
UK neobank Revolut has announced an expansion of its partnership with Serie A football club Como 1907, with Revolut becoming the club’s Official Front-of-Shirt Partner from the 2026/27 season onward. The parties said that the agreement unites two challenger brands that have evolved beyond their core industries to become lifestyle-driven powerhouses, combining innovation, culture, and community to redefine how modern audiences engage with finance and football.

This markets Revolut’s second major European football sponsorship this year, after Revolut signed a deal to become back-of-shirt sponsor for Manchester City back in February. Since the partnership launched in 2025, with Revolut serving as Como 1907’s Global Banking and FX Partner, the two companies have built a robust operational foundation. With Revolut Business fully integrated into its financial operations, Como 1907 manages everything from supplier payments to complex foreign exchange transactions through a single, seamless financial platform.

Competitor News.title: ‘We’re Not Doing It’: Ryan Day Gets Explains Initial Hesitation With Accepting JP Morgan’s Deal With Ohio State
Competitor News.summary: ‘We’re Not Doing It’: Ryan Day Gets Explains Initial Hesitation With Accepting JP Morgan’s Deal With Ohio State College Sports Network
Competitor News.body:
Ohio State Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day had reservations about the team’s deal with JPMorganChase. The deal, which was struck on Tuesday, makes JPMorganChase the official bank sponsor of Ohio State Athletics.

Moreover, the deal sees the bank becoming the first jersey patch sponsor in Buckeyes history. Day initially opposed the idea before one color theme changed his mind. “I do want to say, in full disclosure, when I first heard about this, I knew about the reputation of JPMorganChase, and I was excited. But then I saw the logo, and I said, ‘Absolutely not, we’re not doing this,'” Day told reporters about the conversation he had with Ohio State’s AD Ross Bjork.

Competitor News.title: Jersey Patch Madness Shows Deion Sanders' Value to Colorado Buffaloes
Competitor News.summary: Jersey Patch Madness Shows Deion Sanders' Value to Colorado Buffaloes Sports Illustrated
Competitor News.body:
With the Ohio State Buckeyes reportedly signing a jersey patch deal with JP Morgan Chase worth $17 million annually, the Big 12's conference-wide agreement to add Monster Energy patches for $20 million across 16 schools has been called into question. Shortly after news of Ohio State's deal broke, Notre Dame announced a sponsorship deal with SoFi, reportedly worth $20 million per year, according to insider Ross Dellenger.

In the 2026-27 football and basketball seasons, Colorado Buffaloes fans can expect to see a bright green M patched onto the team's jerseys like the rest of the Big 12. The conference's deal is the first of its kind across college sports, and Monster will reportedly pay a lump sum of $20 million that will be divided across the 16 teams in the Big 12.
